The FTSE 100 posted solid gains on Wednesday after earlier hitting a new all-time high, lifted by well-received earnings and gains in BP and Shell as the oil price strengthened.

The FTSE 100 index closed up 37.39 points, 0.3%, at 10,908.41. It had earlier hit a new intra-day high of 10,951.06, although it ended just short of its all-time record close of 10,910.55, seen in February.

The FTSE 250 ended down slightly at 23,996.81, while the AIM All-Share closed down 6.09 points, 0.8%, at 761.85.

In European equities on Wednesday, the CAC 40 in Paris closed down 0.6%, weighed by falls in luxury goods retailer Hermes, while the DAX 40 in Frankfurt ended down slightly.

Stocks in New York were weaker with fresh falls in technology stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.5%, the S&P 500 index was 0.8% lower, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.1%.

After London’s close, attention will focus on the US interest rate decision at 7pm and earnings from Magnificent Seven members Meta Platforms and Microsoft.

Market pricing puts the chances of the US Federal Reserve raising interest rates at around 34%, making it one of the most uncertain meetings in years.

Much of this can be put down to a lack of forward guidance from new Fed chairman Kevin Warsh. Nonetheless, a clear majority of analysts expect the US central bank to leave rates on hold.

Eric Winograd, senior vice president and director of Developed Market Economic Research, AllianceBernstein, said: “I do not expect the Fed to raise rates this week, and I have not seen any other credible forecaster who thinks that they will do so. That said, it can’t be ruled out.”

“By and large, the case for a rate hike is weaker now than it was at the time of the last Fed meeting,” Mr Winograd said, noting the June inflation and payrolls reports were both soft.

Still, the market is pricing a decent chance of a hike because several members of the Federal Open Market Committee have indicated that they are ready to raise rates and are likely to vote in that direction, whether with a majority or in dissent.

“It is likely that if (Mr Warsh) were to suggest a hike, he would have enough votes to make it happen. He has told us nothing about his willingness or desire to raise rates, so we don’t know if he intends to do so or not. I think probably not, but that uncertainty is reflected in market pricing,” the analyst added.

The pound was lower at 1.3284 dollars on Wednesday afternoon, against 1.3306 dollars at the equities close on Tuesday. Against the euro, sterling was slightly lower at 1.1673 euro from 1.1674 euro.

The euro stood lower at 1.1380 dollars from 1.1397 dollars. Against the yen, the dollar was higher at 163.85 yen, compared to 163.68 yen.

The yield on the US 10-year Treasury stretched to 4.64% on Wednesday from 4.59% on Tuesday. The yield on the US 30-year Treasury widened to 5.12% from 5.09%.

Oil prices surged once more as US President Donald Trump vowed to hit back hard at Iran after it attacked US bases in Jordan on Wednesday.

The warning came after a short lull in the fighting that had spurred hopes of a return to negotiations appeared to draw to an end, sending the price of Brent crude back above 90 dollars.

Brent oil for September delivery traded higher at 90.09 dollars a barrel on Wednesday afternoon, from 84.87 dollars late Tuesday.

The oil price gains boosted oil majors, including FTSE 100 heavyweights BP, up 3.4%, and Shell, up 2.8%.

Gold was lower at 4,011.17 dollars an ounce on Wednesday from 4,035.95 dollars on Tuesday, dragging shares of Fresnillo down 3.2% and Endeavour Mining down 2.8%.

Engineering firm Weir Group led the blue-chip gainers, up 8.7%, after strong first-half results and better-than-expected orders. Accountancy software provider Sage Group closed up 8.8%, after an upbeat trading statement.

Reckitt Benckiser rose 4.3% as it announced a new share buyback and reported like-for-like sales growth picked up in the second quarter, driven by Emerging Markets.

Reckitt, which owns brands such as disinfectant Dettol and throat lozenges Strepsils, said like-for-like sales growth was 4.7% in its second quarter, beating the 3.6% Visible Alpha consensus cited by RBC Capital Markets. Price/mix grew by 3.2% and volumes by 1.5% – both ahead of forecast. Core Reckitt LFL sales grew 4.2% in the quarter, beating the 3.6% consensus.

RBC analyst James Edwardes Jones said results were “fine, or maybe better than fine given that there was a fear amongst investors of full year downgrades”.

Asia-focused bank Standard Chartered was also in the green, up 2.9%, after it hailed a “record first half performance”, announced a 1 billion dollar buyback and raised guidance.

It now expects operating income growth year-on-year for 2026 to be around the middle of its 5% to 7% range at constant currency, excluding “material notable items”.

On the FTSE 250, Greggs pleased shareholders, jumping 18%, as it reported half-year sales and profit ahead of expectations.

Shares in the Newcastle bakery and fast food chain soared 17% as it said pre-tax profit improved 20% to £76 million in the 26 weeks to June 27 from £63.5 million a year before, with revenue up 7.2% to £1.1 billion from £1.03 billion, beating £73.1 million and £1.09 billion consensus, respectively, as cited by JPMorgan.

Operating profit increased 23% to £86.5 million from £70.4 million, ahead of the £79.0 million consensus.

The biggest risers on the FTSE 100 were Sage Group, up 82.2p at 1,022p; Weir Group, up 220p at 2,744p; Burberry, up 53p at 1,193p; Reckitt Benckiser, up 224p at 5,400p; and BP, up 17.8p at 543.5p.

The biggest fallers on the FTSE 100 were Aberdeen, down 10.6p at 238p; Diploma, down 310p at 7,110p; IMI, down 114p at 2,860p; Halma, down 120p at 3,410p; and Fresnillo, down 120p at 2,481p.

Thursday’s economic calendar includes the UK interest rate decision, eurozone unemployment and GDP data, and a US GDP reading.

Thursday’s UK corporate calendar sees a slew of half-year results, including those from miner Anglo American, pest control specialist Rentokil, lender Lloyds Banking Group and aerospace company Rolls-Royce.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool move 'agreed', Vinicius Jr to Arsenal, Marcus Rashford swap
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news from Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and more as they look to improve their teams ahead of the Premier League season

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Wednesday, July 29th.

There is little over a month remaining of the transfer window as clubs continue their preparations for the new season. Already, two deals worth more than £100million have been completed, with Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea from Aston Villa and Elliot Anderson making the switch from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City.

They may not yet prove to be the biggest deals of the summer. Vinicius Junior's future at Real Madrid remains unresolved, and Arsenal are willing to move for the Brazilian if the opportunity arises.

The Gunners are prepared to offer the star the biggest deal in their history, but also want to improve in other areas. Their interest in Bruno Guimaraes is still causing plenty of drama as Newcastle deny any suggestion of advanced talks for the midfielder.

Liverpool are still looking to delve into the market, with new boss Andoni Iraola keen to land a winger. Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola remains of interest.

Manchester United have already landed two midfielders, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, in recent weeks but could still add another. The futures of Marcus Rashford and striker Joshua Zirkzee could still lie away from Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup

With Gianni Infantino plotting to turn the World Cup into a business where shares can be bought and sold, the Premier League have issued their response

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's idea with the World Cup has evoked plenty of ire (Image: 2026 Alex Livesey - Danehouse)

The Premier League has publicly objected to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors. He unveiled plans to launch a company called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) which would bring the sale of FIFA's commercial rights together.

‌



After going through his idea, the Premier League issued a statement backing the position laid out by the European Leagues, which firmly expressed its opposition to Infantino's plan. The top flight of English football wrote: "The Premier League is a founder member of the European Leagues and fully supports this statement."

‌



The European Leagues issued a statement which read: "FIFA’s announcement that its President is pursuing private investment options for a new subsidiary, consolidating its commercial and event-related operations, represents a reckless and divisive development for world football. The World Cup should not be for sale.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"It is not FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal. Football’s success has always been built on a pyramidal open structure and the delicate balance between domestic and international football. Commercial opportunities must support these foundations, not risk altering them.

"This opaque process and unilateral proposal are part of a long-term pattern in FIFA’s decision-making – a pattern which prompted the European Leagues to lodge a complaint with the European Commission on the basis that FIFA’s imposition of decisions on the international match calendar constitutes an abuse of dominant position that violates European competition law.

‌



"Proposals relating to calendar and competitions, should be developed through transparent, accountable and inclusive processes, with meaningful engagement and consent from all stakeholders whose interests are affected, as explicitly requested by the Court of Justice of the EU in its 2023 Super League ruling.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"We have held productive meetings with the European Commission about this matter and have confidence that the legal decisions they take will continue to be in the best interests of fans and football communities.

‌



"European Leagues will continue to work with UEFA to safeguard the long-term interests of the game. We have faith that Federations/National Associations around the world will do the same as they scrutinise this proposal from the FIFA President."

It's understood Infantino has informed all of FIFA's 211 member associations they must agree to his World Cup sell-off plan by September 19 if they want the funding, which is believed to be around £30m for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, which will also include a one-off windfall of £15m in January next year.

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino watched South Korea take on Czech Republic at the Guadalajara Stadium in Zapopan (Image: (Ulises RUIZ / AFP via Getty Images))

‌



UEFA president Alexander Ceferin is expected to amass the European governing body's 55 member nations, amid calls for a mass boycott of FIFA in response to the plan. However, Czechian Football Association president David Trunda has already offered his support for Infantino's plan.

He said: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team. Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

The proposal has received huge backing from Thrive Capital, who are part owned by Joshua Kusher whose brother Jared is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump.

Sports.title: Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has told FIFA’s 211 member associations to sign up to his World Cup sell-off plans by mid-September - or say goodbye to the prospect of almost $7.5billion in extra funding.

The plotting FIFA president has sent a letter to the associations, saying: “Should you wish to proceed, this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together. Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme (development money) of $2.7billion as previously presented.”

Infantino has given members until September 19 to accept his proposal which, he promises, will see them get $40million for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, starting with a one-off windfall of $20million in January, 2027.

Infantino knows that a lot of the associations will be tempted by the extra cash but his letter has produced a furious response from UEFA.

‌



UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In its latest statement, UEFA said: “We have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan

“But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.”

Aleksander Ceferin, the UEFA president, will today chair a meeting of its 55 member nations amidst growing calls for a European boycott of the World Cup and Club World Cup if Infantino’s scheme gets the go-ahead.

‌



But UEFA unity is far from guaranteed, with the president of the Czech Republic’s football association, David Trunda, already saying: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team.

“Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

Trunda’s praise of the scheme - which would see a private company with links to the extended family of Donald Trump run FIFA competitions - is against most opinions voiced so far. But the Football Association were typically guarded in their mildly critical response.

‌



A statement read: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached. Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

The Welsh response was even more non-committal, with a FAW statement saying: “The Football Association of Wales has not yet received any substantial details from FIFA concerning the reported proposals.

“Consequently, the FAW is concerned that such matters have become public prior to being shared with FIFA’s Member Associations. We await receipt of FIFA’s full proposal before commenting further on this matter.”

‌



Despite a huge backlash, led in England by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, sources close to Infantino say he is hell-bent on getting the scheme voted through.

And now it remains to be seen if UEFA follow up their tough words with equally tough action.

Sports.title: England must boycott the Women's World Cup to stop Gianni Infantino selling football's soul
Sports.content:
Just when you thought Gianni Infantino had finally exhausted the depths of administrative sleaze, FIFA's supreme leader has managed to discover a brand new basement underneath the trapdoor.

For a decade now, the world's most preening, Teflon-coated football bureaucrat has glided through global corridors of power like a smoothly oiled Bond villain - a man whose moral compass spins so wildly it could unclog a backed-up sewer pipe... and it's little wonder, given nobody on earth is quite so proficient at unleashing fresh torrents of corporate cr*p upon the world.

We've watched him turn world football into a travelling circus of shameless sycophancy and endless cash-grabs. But his latest stunt isn't just another piece of administrative vandalism. It's an outright heist on the very soul of the game.

Infantino's latest brainwave is as brazen as it is grotesque: he wants to carve off FIFA's commercial rights - broadcasting, ticketing, licensing, the lot - and sell a 20 per cent stake in a new entity, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to private equity investors for $4.2billion (£3.16bn).

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed READ MORE :

And who, pray tell, is leading this financial feeding frenzy? An investment group fronted by Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law. You genuinely couldn't write a script this eye-rollingly absurd.

This, lest we forget, comes right on the heels of the 2026 World Cup, where Infantino spent two months performing a series of breathtaking contortions to stay in President Trump's good books. We saw the ultimate humiliation when Trump personally phoned Infantino to complain about a red card shown to USA striker Folarin Balogun; lo and behold, FIFA's "independent" judicial committee magically suspended the ban.

Now, having allowed Trump to rewrite the rulebook on the fly, Infantino is handing the keys to the commercial treasury over to the President's extended family network. And to ensure nobody asks too many awkward questions, Infantino is dangling a £30million cash bribe in front of every national association, telling them to sign off on the sell-off by September 19 or risk losing their grassroots funding. It's classic mob-style governance: accept the envelope of cash, keep your mouth shut, and let the suit-and-tie vultures pick the bones clean.

‌



So, how has our very own Football Association responded to this existential assault on the game? On cue, Wembley's blazer-clad technocrats duly gathered in a softly lit boardroom, wrung their hands, and issued a statement expressing "deep concern." It's the administrative equivalent of throwing a soggy tissue at a roaring fire. Next up, perhaps they'll design a nice, polite lapel badge or a colourful warm-up top to really show how much they disapprove.

View 3 Images The way Infantino has cosied up to Donald Trump encapsulates the rot inside FIFA (Image: Getty Images)

We've seen this limp, hand-wringing film before. In Qatar, it was a brief, panicked flutter over rainbow armbands that vanished the second a yellow card was mentioned. In North America, it was polite, muted murmurs while Infantino effectively turned the World Cup draw into a political rally. The FA's idea of taking a stand usually has all the backbone of a jellyfish. They make polite noises in Zurich committee rooms, take their allocated seats in the VIP boxes, and watch quietly as Infantino counts his billfolds.

Enough. No more virtue-signalling. No more sternly worded press releases that Infantino uses to line his shredder. If Mark Bullingham and the FA genuinely care about protecting football from being auctioned off to private equity speculators and political cronies, they must reach for the nuclear button: England must threaten an immediate, total boycott of the 2027 Women's World Cup.

‌



And they shouldn't do it alone. They must immediately form an impenetrable European front alongside UEFA allies - Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands - and deliver a blunt, non-negotiable ultimatum. Either Infantino withdraws the FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme permanently and bans private equity from owning commercial stakes in international tournaments, or he can watch the 2027 tournament implode without a single European team stepping onto the pitch.

Without the Lionesses, without defending champions Spain, and without the rest of Europe's elite, Infantino's shiny $20bn pitch to Wall Street collapses overnight. Private equity sharks do not invest billions in empty stadiums, depleted TV ratings, and second-rate substitute teams. Cut off the star power, and the money-men will scatter back into the shadows faster than you can say "conflict of interest."

View 3 Images The FA must boycott the Women's World Cup next year (Image: Getty Images)

We know this strategy works because we've seen the terrifying magic of righteous football fury before. Cast your mind back to the European Super League heist in 2021: a cartel of greedy billionaires attempting to ring-fence the sport, only to be completely obliterated within 48 hours by a tidal wave of fan power.

‌



When supporters took to the streets, blocked team buses, and made the ground shake beneath the owners' feet, those ruthless corporate conquerors folded like cheap deckchairs. If the FA's suits lack the spine to lead the charge against Infantino's privatised empire, then the fans must force their hand and light the touch paper once more.

For too long, football's spineless custodians have treated Gianni Infantino like bad weather - an unpleasant, unavoidable tax on existence to be endured under a squeaking umbrella while he quietly auctions off the family silver.

Well, the World Cup is not a sovereign kingdom, Infantino is not its feudal lord, and the global game does not belong to Wall Street suit-wearers or Florida golf club courtiers. It belongs to the terraces, the muddy park pitches, and the millions around the world who pour their lives into it.

The line in the sand is drawn, the fuse is lit, and the time for polite diplomatic bowing is over. The FA must finally grow a spine, grab the sledgehammer, and smash this corrupt racket to splinters before there is nothing left to save.

‌

Sports.title: UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan
Sports.content:
UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan

UEFA are firmly opposed to Gianni Infantino and FIFA's controversial plan to sell shares in its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors and have issued another statement

View Image FIFA is at war with UEFA (Image: Pau BARRENA/AFP via Getty Images)

UEFA has issued a second statement criticising FIFA's plan to sell off the World Cup, saying that the scheme is designed to 'enrich themselves and their friends'. It comes ahead of an emergency UEFA meeting which will see European football chiefs discuss FIFA President Gianni Infantino's plan to sell shares in its competitions to private investors.

‌



After the plans were leaked on Tuesday, UEFA issued a statement claiming that FIFA had 'crossed a line'. Now, further reports say that FIFA has written to its 211 member associations promising $40m (£30m) if they back the controversial plan.

‌



It's added that the members have until September 19 to respond positively - or else they will not get to access an initial $20m (£15m) by January 1. UEFA have said that the deadline 'says everything you need to know about this plan'.

‌



A statement read: "Today we have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.

"We can grow the game correctly. It's time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans."

‌



At the upcoming emergency meeting, UEFA could discuss boycotting the World Cup in what would be a drastic move. UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin missed the men's final earlier this month amid tensions with FIFA. The next World Cup on the calendar is the women's edition in Brazil next year.

It should be noted that FIFA is a not-for-profit organisation and is owned by its 211 members. FIFA therefore enjoys a tax-free status in Switzerland, where its headquarters are located.

FIFA insist that, in the event of outside investment, it would retain sole control over football governance, its competitions and the international match calendar, as well as all sporting and regulatory decisions. It adds that the investment would go into a FIFA subsidiary rather than FIFA itself.

‌



Infantino commented in FIFA's announcement - made after its plan was leaked: "Football is the world's most popular sport and an extraordinary engine of human and social development.

"Parts of the game have turned that popularity into remarkable commercial value - and we celebrate that success and want it to continue, because it lifts the whole game ... our next stage of growth needs a structure built for it, one where the commercial side of the game operates as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world."

Sports.title: Abandoned EFL stadium set to be demolished 18 years after former club left
Sports.content:
Abandoned EFL stadium set to be demolished 18 years after former club left

The ground is in a sorry state after falling into disrepair

View 3 Images Millmoor has been largely untouched since Rotherham United left in 2008 (Image: Getty Images)

An abandoned EFL ground could finally be demolished, almost 20 years since it last hosted a men's football match. Millmoor was the home of Rotherham United from 1907 until 2008 and hosted some of the club's most memorable moments.

‌



Due to disputes over the ownership and redevelopment of the ground, the Millers left the stadium in 2008 with a view to building a new ground in the town. They moved temporarily to the Don Valley athletics stadium in Sheffield, an unloved venue because of its running track.

‌



The club eventually bought land close to Millmoor to build their new home, the 12,000-capacity New York Stadium, which opened in 2012. Meanwhile, Millmoor, which is clearly visible from the new ground on the other side of a railway line, has remained largely untouched since 2008.

‌



It looked set to get a second life in 2024, when it was spruced up by Ken Booth Jr, the son of long-time owner Ken Booth. The site was revamped and cleared of debris so it could be used by local junior teams and the Doncaster Belles women's team.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

But two years on, the historic venue could now be torn down after the ground's owners, CF Booth, entered administration, with the Ron Hull Group acquiring Millmoor.

‌



Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed READ MORE :

A statement by the Ron Hull Group, issued via the Rotherham Business News, read: "The buildings and structures selected in the current application to demolish are all in a poor condition due to years of neglect and are suffering from a general lack of maintenance, specifically elements like roof finishes and the structures themselves.

"It is assumed this situation accelerated in the period since Rotherham United Football Club vacated the site.

View 3 Images The abandoned stadium had been left to the elements (Image: Ben Booth/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



"The current main stand is only partially completed, and has been exposed to the elements since at least 2007.

"The high cost of repair, yet alone proceed to complete this stand would be excessive given that there are very limited numbers of possible users of the ground. Thus meaning it is unbuyable."

View 3 Images The ground could be no more by early next year (Image: Ben Booth/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



If the demolition plan is approved by the local authority, the Millmoor Lane and Railway stand, plus adjoining buildings, will be levelled, with work expected to conclude by the end of January 2027.

The Millers are preparing for life in League Two after suffering relegation from League One last season.

Sports.title: Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer
Sports.content:
Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer

Jordan Henderson had one year left on his contract with Brentford, but the club have agreed to terminate his deal in order for him to join Chelsea on a free transfer

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is on his way to Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Brentford have announced the departure of Jordan Henderson, paving the way for him to join Chelsea. Henderson, 36, is poised to move to Stamford Bridge on a free transfer after Brentford agreed to terminate his contract.

‌



The former Liverpool captain signed a two-year deal with Keith Andrews' side in July 2025 but has cut short his stay after a single season. As Brentford confirmed his exit, Henderson said: "I leave Brentford with a lot of gratitude for the opportunity the club gave me, and for the support and care shown to me and my family from day one.

‌



"Coming back to the Premier League was really important to me, and Brentford gave me that chance. I'll always be thankful for that. I hope I was able to play my part in helping the team through an important period for the club. We achieved a lot together last season, and it’s something everyone involved should be proud of.

‌



"Brentford is a special football club. It's ambitious, progressive and full of good people. From the owners and leadership, to the coaching staff, the players and everyone behind the scenes, it's been a privilege to be part of it.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest READ MORE :

"Most of all, I'd like to thank the supporters. Their backing never changed, and the connection they have with the club is clear to see. They care deeply about Brentford and they support the team in the right way every step of the journey.

‌



"Finally, thank you to Matt (Benham, owner), Phil (Giles, director of football), Lee (Dykes, technical director) and Keith, every member of staff, and all my team-mates. It's been a pleasure to work alongside you, and I'll look back on my time at Brentford with a lot of pride and some great memories."

Henderson made 36 appearances for Brentford, helping them secure a ninth-place finish in the Premier League. The midfielder had spent the previous 18 months at Ajax following a spell in Saudi Arabia which came after 12 trophy-laden years at Liverpool, winning both the Premier League title and one Champions League trophy.

Andrews commented: "Following the departure of our club captain Christian Norgaard to Arsenal, and with Vitaly Janelt not fit enough to start the season, Jordan was a really important signing for us because he added elite-level experience.

‌



Will Jordan Henderson be a good signing for Chelsea? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson played for England at the World Cup (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

"He played a big part in some memorable performances, especially in the early part of the season as we were forming a new team. He had an insatiable desire to represent England at the World Cup in the summer and it was always part of the plan for us to discuss the next chapter for him and what it looked like.

Article continues below

"Taking into consideration Jordan's ambitions and where our squad is currently, we both felt it was the right time for Jordan to pursue his career elsewhere. It's been a pleasure working with Jordan and I sincerely wish him every success."

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership A-Z guide for the new season!
Sports.content:
The new Scottish Premiership season is back with a bang!

Every single game across the opening weekend will be shown live on Sky Sports, starting with Rangers' trip to Dundee United on Friday, and ending with Celtic against Dundee on Monday.

Scottish Premiership live on Sky Sports this weekend Friday: Dundee Utd vs Rangers | From 7pm, kick-off 8pm

Saturday: Falkirk vs St Mirren | From 2pm, kick-off 3pm

Saturday: Aberdeen vs Hearts | From 5.15pm, kick-off 5.30pm

Sunday: St Johnstone vs Kilmarnock | From 1pm, kick-off 2pm

Sunday: Hibernian vs Motherwell | From 4pm, kick-off 4.30pm

Monday: Celtic vs Dundee | From 6.30pm, kick-off 7.30pm

Following one of the best seasons ever, as Celtic clinched the title on the final day against Hearts, there are new managers, players, rules and much more to look out for during the campaign.

Ahead of the big kick-off, here's an A-Z of everything that's new about the league this year...

A - Astroturf: There's only one artificial surface left. Kilmarnock have switched to grass at Rugby Park and Livingston have been relegated, so the Falkirk Stadium is the only plastic pitch.

B - Broken Hearts: After losing out on a first top-flight title in 66 years on the final day last season, the squad has been broken up. Captain Lawrence Shankland departed for Rangers one year into a three-year deal. Head coach Derek McInnes followed, before influential midfielder Cammy Devlin made the trip to Ibrox too after rejecting a new Tynecastle deal.

C - Captains: Aberdeen, Hearts, Kilmarnock, Rangers and St Mirren all have new players wearing the armband this year following the departures of Graeme Shinnie, Lawrence Shankland, Brad Lyons, James Tavernier and Mark O'Hara.

Image: Lawrence Shankland is the new Rangers captain

D - Deadline Day: The Scottish Premiership transfer window closes on September 3 at 5pm, that's two days after the Premier League window. So if you're worried that your club hasn't made enough signings yet, don't worry, you've still got well over a month to go.

E - Europe: Five Scottish clubs started out competing in European qualifiers this summer but this year it's a race for the top four, as it's almost certain that Scotland's faltering coefficient ranking will cost one place.

F - Flag days: Champions Celtic will raise the league flag once again when they take on Dundee in the final game of opening weekend on Monday. Newly promoted St Johnstone will also raise the Championship flag at home to Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic won the Scottish Premiership on the final day last season

G - Gordon: This will be the first time since the maiden year of the SPFL in 2013 in which there will be no Craig Gordon in Scotland. The 43-year-old Hearts legend announced his retirement from football following Scotland's exit from the World Cup, 25 years on from making his professional debut.

H - Hogh: Celtic have broken their transfer record to sign Bodo Glimt striker Kasper Hogh for £11m plus add-ons. The Denmark international has been brought in to replace Daizen Maeda, who departed for Ipswich.

I - International breaks: We've just had the World Cup but be prepared for an almost three-week-long break over September and October. The international match calendar has changed from three international windows to just two for this year.

J - Johansson: Motherwell's new boss Alfred Johansson has big shoes to fill after Jens Berthel Askou left for Toulouse. He's the youngest manager in the league at just 35.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson is preparing for his first Scottish Premiership match against Hibernian on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

K - Kenobi: Did you know that Aberdeen's new left back Nesta Guinness-Walker is the great-grandson of Sir Alec Guinness, who played Obi-Wan Kenobi in the original Star Wars trilogy?

L - Law changes: Just as we saw at the World Cup, VAR can now intervene on second yellow cards. Meanwhile, players will have a five-second countdown to take throw-ins and goal kicks, while there is just 10 seconds for a substitute to leave the field, plus a minute break for those who undergo treatment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gordon Duncan explains the new VAR changes ahead of the beginning of the new Scottish Premiership season

M - McInnes: For the fifth season in a row, Rangers start with a new manager. Derek McInnes is tasked with doing what the last five permanent Rangers bosses failed to do, win the league title.

N - New mascot: St Johnstone are looking for someone new to take on the role of Brogan the Beagle after the previous Brogan hung up the paws after 11 years.

O - O'Neill: At 74 years old, Martin O'Neill is back at Celtic for what is technically his fourth spell. He won a league and cup double last term after replacing Brendan Rodgers, then Wilfried Nancy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin O’Neill says Celtic will bring more players in as he speaks about club-record signing Kasper Høgh

P - Promoted: St Johnstone are back in the Premiership after a year out. They're the only newly promoted side after St Mirren beat Partick Thistle in the play-off final in May.

Q - Questionable haircuts: New season means new trim but Falkirk's League Cup trialist David Ninkovic will take some beating!

Image: David Ninkovic was on trial at Falkirk

R - Robinson's rebuild: Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson is about to begin his first full season at Pittodrie. Staying with Aberdeen, R is also for Rachel Corsie. The Sky Sports pundit and former Scotland captain has been appointed to the club's Board of Directors.

S - Six: The number of games on opening weekend live on Sky Sports. Yes, that's right, all 12 clubs will be shown live on the home of Scottish football on the same weekend for the very first time.

Scottish Premiership live on Sky Sports this weekend Friday: Dundee Utd vs Rangers | From 7pm, kick-off 8pm

Saturday: Falkirk vs St Mirren | From 2pm, kick-off 3pm

Saturday: Aberdeen vs Hearts | From 5.15pm, kick-off 5.30pm

Sunday: St Johnstone vs Kilmarnock | From 1pm, kick-off 2pm

Sunday: Hibernian vs Motherwell | From 4pm, kick-off 4.30pm

Monday: Celtic vs Dundee | From 6.30pm, kick-off 7.30pm

T - Transfers: The 12 Premiership clubs have made more than 80 new signings already, and there is still more than a month left until the window closes.

U - Ultras: Love them or loath them, all 12 Premiership clubs now have dedicated ultras groups, aiming to bring more passion and noise to the stands.

V - Vrancken: Hearts have chosen Wouter Vrancken as the man to replace Derek McInnes and put up a title fight once more. He was named Belgian manager of the year last year and came within minutes of winning the league with Genk in 2023.

W - World Cup: The new Premiership season kicks off just 12 days after the World Cup final. Winners Spain sadly didn't have anyone from our league in their squad, but there are two new Spaniards in the division. Unax Alvarez at St Johnstone and Samuel Ramos at St Mirren.

X - Xperience: Yes, a bit of cheating here! But Motherwell captain Paul McGinn is now the oldest player in the division at 35, that's the same age as his manager Alfred Johansson!

Y - Years: It's now been 41 years since a non-Old Firm club won the league. Hearts took it to the final day last year, can they, or someone else, mount a challenge this time?

Z - Zero: That's the number of Scottish Premiership games which will not be live on Sky Sports this weekend. It all starts at Tannadice on Friday night as Rangers take on Dundee Utd.

Sports.title: Bow Echo roars home late to seal Sussex Stakes success
Sports.content:
Bow Echo’s dazzling turn of foot once again came to the fore as he came out on top in an epic renewal of the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes.

George Boughey's unbeaten colt was a brilliant winner of the 2000 Guineas before overcoming adversity to register a workmanlike victory in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and was the 10-11 favourite to complete a famous hat-trick at Goodwood last achieved by the one and only Frankel in 2011.

It was again not an easy watch for odds-on backers, with Bow Echo stuck in the middle of the pack with plenty of work to do as the race began in earnest, but he ultimately went through the gears in stunning fashion in the final half-furlong to get up and beat his old rival Gstaad by half a length.

Boughey said: "He's got an explosive turn of foot, it was probably a bit messier than we might have thought with the gallop they went.

"Huge credit to Billy again for being ice cool. He's an extraordinary horseman and rider to go with it and Billy producing the horse like he is is just phenomenal.

"But fundamentally what an animal. The constitution to have another rough race, relax through it then find the line as strong as he did - I'm lost for words really.

"He's so fast, he's like a motorbike. He stays the mile, but has an exceptional turn of foot to go with it. Billy has had tremendous belief in this horse for a long time and so have I.

"We knew what happened at Ascot and it was just having the confidence to take stock and go again. I always thought this was the race for him, we had to get him back from what was a hard race (at Royal Ascot), but he's shown how good he is there.

"It was always going to be messy, a Sussex Stakes with 12 runners. But it was to the letter how we wanted to ride the horse. There were a few gaps that closed and Billy had to sit tight and come round, but it was brilliant."

Image: Billy Loughnane celebrates Sussex Stakes glory aboard Bow Echo

Emulating Frankel with his Newmarket, Ascot and Goodwood treble is an achievement that gives his handler overwhelming pride.

Boughey added: "It's not lost on me what he has achieved this year and it dawned on the last few days I might never be in this position again. There are a lot of trainers who have trained a lot better horses than I have who haven't been in this position.

"It's desperately sad Sheikh Mohammed Obaid isn't here to see him and this is 30-plus years of work to get here.

"I can't put into words what this horse means to me and he's a warrior as well as being a very fast horse."

Having delighted on home soil, he could now head on his travels.

Boughey said: "The plan was either to go to France for the Prix Jacques le Marois or the Prix du Moulin. We would love for the horse to end up in a Breeders' Cup Mile at the end of the year and I think round a bend in America off a strong pace will suit him well."

Loughnane said: "They made life difficult for him, but I always wanted to follow Ryan (Moore, on Gstaad), that was my plan.

"I knew the pace would be on with the set-up of the race. I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe (Soumillon, on Puerto Rico) and I just had to wait to get out. But once I did, he proved how good he is."

Flora Of Bermuda finds seven furlongs to her liking

Flora Of Bermuda landed a first win over seven furlongs to open new routes in Group company when outclassing her rivals in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes.

The Andrew Balding-trained filly had previously plied her trade almost exclusively at six furlongs, placing at Group One level and winning the Group Three Summer Stakes at York last time out.

But opportunities at both six and seven furlongs now beckon for the five-year-old after she produced a solid performance as the 5-2 favourite to land this Group Three contest by a neck from Sayidah Dariyan with Radiant Beauty third.

The Wathnan Racing-owned Flora Of Bermuda sat in sixth place as Zanthos cut out the early running but after starting to make ground at the cutaway, she took it up at the furlong pole and stayed on strongly to the line.

Image: Flora Of Bermuda struck gold at Goodwood

Balding said: "We've been thinking about seven furlongs for a bit and this seemed an obvious place to try it.

"She's been very consistent at a high level throughout her career and is a fantastic filly. She's done very well physically this year, she has to go in the stalls late and if she has any flaw it is she is not very patient, she'll go in the stalls OK but just won't stand there for any longer than 30 seconds.

"Ascot was a bit of a disaster and she fluffed the start, but other than that she is three from three this year.

"You can't really go abroad with her because of the stalls, she will probably go to the City of York Stakes or the Haydock Sprint Cup. It would be great to win a Group One with her one day and I think if everything drops right for her one time she will.

"She's amazingly versatile and won the Alice Keppel here on heavy ground and then a few years later this on fast ground."

Wild Blossom takes another step forward

Bigger and better things may await Wild Blossom after her taking victory in the British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes.

Karl Burke's Wathnan Racing-owned filly came into the race having finished 10th in the Queen Mary, although that run was better than the placing suggested as she was only beaten four and a half lengths.

Under James Doyle she was the 5-4 favourite to make good on the promise shown at Royal Ascot, and did so with little fuss, prevailing by a length and a half from Andrew Balding's Fast Track.

"She worked with a very good older filly last week and worked very nicely," said Burke.

"It is just a slight concern when they do it so well first time on slow ground, then she ran very well at Ascot where the draw completely scuppered her really.

"This was the plan since Ascot. I don't know, we'll look at all those Group five-furlong races, she's a very quick filly.

"I wouldn't dismiss six furlongs, we'll see what James says, but that was the plan.

"There's no real future targets at the moment, the Flying Childers at Doncaster, races like that."

Connections of Infraad were made to wait for confirmation of their victory in the opening Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap, but were eventually thrilled to see William Haggas' improving colt keep the race after a stewards' inquiry.

Tom Marquand's mount was sent off the 2-1 favourite and edged out Andrew Balding's well-regarded 9-4 market rival Hatteen for a head success after a late duel between the two lightly-raced three-year-olds.

Maureen Haggas, assistant to her husband, said: "You never know these days what they will do, but I could imagine it took so long because Tom and Oisin (Murphy) were in the same room and they are quite good talkers and they couldn't stop them.

"He needed every inch of the mile and a half and it would not surprise me if he goes a bit further in time. He's a work in progress and he's going the right way. He's got his act together today and hopefully he keeps progressing."

Sports.title: O'Neill promises more Celtic signings | McGregor: Where I want to be
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill insists there is "no question" that Celtic will make more signings this summer, but he wants "quality rather than quantity".

The Scottish Premiership champions have brought in Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh so far, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain returning on a new one-year deal.

Supporters have been frustrated by the club's lack of transfer activity, while influential striker Daizen Maeda has left to join newly-promoted Premier League side Ipswich Town.

Celtic begin their title defence against Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports, ahead of their Champions League play-off later this month.

But manager O'Neill is urging some patience from fans.

"We're trying to get some quality into the football club," the 74-year-old told Sky Sports News.

"We've lost Daizen, he was a big, big player for us and so we have to replace him. I think that we're doing our best to do that.

"We will get some more players in, there's no question about that, but I want quality rather than quantity."

Image: Camilo Duran has joined Celtic on a five-year deal

After a rollercoaster campaign that saw O'Neill return to the club twice, Celtic clinched the title in a final-day decider against Hearts in May.

And O'Neill wants the players to take some lessons into the new campaign.

"Last season was terrific, it's gone now, it's consigned to history. Now we're ready to go," he added.

"I think it was mentality as much as anything else that got us over the line.

"It was strong, it was a will to win and we saw it through.

"That will be very, very important this season, there's no question about that."

McGregor: Where I want to be

Meanwhile, Callum McGregor has reiterated that Celtic is "where I want to be" amid ongoing speculation linking the long-serving captain with a reunion with former boss Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia.

The 33-year-old said in April he wanted the club to match his ambitions if he was to stay on as they laboured towards the Scottish Premiership title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic captain Callum McGregor discusses his future, hope for signings and the Champions League target | Watch Celtic vs Dundee, live on Sky on Monday

"Listen, this is a football club that's been part of my whole life since I was eight, nine years old. It's where I want to be. It's where I want to play football," he said.

"Ultimately, I want to keep driving everything that I possibly can to make sure this club is successful. Then eventually, the day that you do leave it, you want to leave it in a really good place."

Asked if he felt the club were matching his ambitions, McGregor said: "Yes, listen, we've signed two strikers, two really good players. Obviously, they've come in and done really well.

"Big Kasper (Hogh) has just joined us over the last 24 hours. It's good signs, it's positive steps and that is to add to what is a really good group already.

"I spoke about this at the end of the season as well. I don't really think there's a group of players and a group of staff that could have got us through that difficult moment as much as these boys did.

"It's obviously about trying to add bits of quality, but what we do have here is guys who want to work for the club, who are good footballers, who want to get better and ultimately did bring success to the football club during a difficult season, so we have the makings of a really, really good team.

"Obviously, the standard for us is trying to get to Champions League football. That's where we want to be. It takes the club to a different level. So, can we keep pushing as players, staff and our football club to make sure we get there?"

Celtic begin title defence against Dundee

Celtic begin their Scottish Premiership title defence at home to Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports.

The Monday night clash, which will kick-off at 7.30pm, rounds off a groundbreaking opening weekend that will see all six top-flight games shown live on Sky Sports for the first time.

Sports.title: Ko reveals plan to 'channel inner Foxy' in push for more major glory
Sports.content:
Lydia Ko wants to "channel her inner Foxy" and push for more New Zealand major success at the AIG Women's Open, having been reduced to tears by Ryan Fox's win at The Open.

Fox claimed a dramatic one-shot win at Royal Birkdale earlier this month, where a final-hole birdie saw him become only the third men's major champion from New Zealand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment New Zealand's Ryan Fox won The Open with a 12-foot birdie on the final hole

The 39-year-old's win was the first New Zealand success at The Open since Bob Charles lifted the Claret Jug in 1963 at Royal Lytham & St Annes, the same venue where Ko will chase a fourth major title and second AIG Women's Open victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of The Open, where Fox claimed a dramatic victory at Royal Birkdale

"I would love to keep the dice rolling," Ko said in her pre-tournament press conference. "Super-excited for Foxy [Ryan Fox] and the whole of golf in New Zealand for his win just up the road at Royal Birkdale.

"I don't think I've been that nervous and that excited watching somebody else play. Just his whole back nine and the way he played over the weekend was incredible.

"It would be cool to channel my inner Foxy and his fearlessness out there these next few days."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Fox's winning round at The Open, where a two-under 68 saw him complete major victory

Fox had been eight strokes off the halfway lead before equalling men's major history with a third-round 62, leaving him two back heading into the final day. He then birdied two of his last three holes to close out the major victory.

"I went to go work out and everywhere I went I was like 'please turn on The Open'," added Ko, who was watching Fox's win from the west coast of the USA. "It ended up not working on the TV, so I had it on my cell phone.

Image: Lydia Ko is looking to win her fourth major title the AIG Women's Open

"I can't remember my workout at all because my whole focus was there. I took an Uber ride back home. As soon as I got home he was on the 18th - when I saw that drive I was relieved but so excited, super-pumped.

"I went in, I closed the door and I screamed. My husband ran out and was like 'what's happening?' Ten seconds later, I was just crying. It was emotional for me. I can only imagine what it was like for him!"

Image: Ko's last worldwide win was at the 2025 HSBC Women's World Championship

Ko missed the cut in the first two women's majors of the year before recovering from a slow start to the KPMG Women's PGA Championship to finish tied-15th, then shared seventh at the Amundi Evian Championship.

The 29-year-old plays alongside Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu - both multiple major winners in 2026 - over the first two rounds at the AIG Women's Open, with Ko aware of the challenging test ahead as she looks to lift the trophy for a second time in three years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ko carded a final-round 69 to claim major victory in the 2024 AIG Women's Open at St Andrews

"I think it [winning] would be very special," Ko said. "I think this is the toughest Women's Open I have ever played. I don't know what I thought when I played in 2018 - might have been in a lot of bunkers that are on the golf course that are in my memory bank.

"It actually feels like a very new course to me. I know they made a little bit of adjustments on a couple of the holes, but it's a hard golf course. Even on a pretty perfect day it's playing hard. So when you win on that kind of calibre of golf course, I think it's always something that you come off feeling extra proud.

"With Foxy having won The Open, I think it [winning] would be very meaningful and I think very empowering for golf in New Zealand."

Sports.title: Tottenham beat Sydney FC on penalties after stunning Tel free-kick
Sports.content:
Tottenham beat Sydney FC on penalties to earn their third victory of pre-season after being held to a 1-1 draw over 90 minutes during which Mathys Tel scored a stunning free-kick.

Tel found the top-right corner with a wonderful strike from 25 yards in the 29th minute in Sydney, but the A-League side equalised after half-time through Takahiro Sekine before Martin Dubravka saved a penalty in the shoot-out, which allowed Dane Scarlett to net the winner.

Tottenham are interested in signing Manchester City winger Savinho and Tel, who only signed for the club permanently this summer in a £30m deal from Bayern Munich, appeared to respond to those transfer links with a stand-out 45-minute display off the left.

How Spurs lined up Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Dubravka; Tye Hall (Robertson, 65), Hardy (Tingey, 78), Davies (Takai, 46), Kyerematen (Byrne, 78); Gray (Donley, 65), Bergvall (Tonali, 46); Solomon (Yang, 65), Gallagher (Melia, 65), Tel (Williams-Barnett, 46); Richarlison (Scarlett, 65)

Unused subs: Kinsky, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Ajayi.

Rested key players: James Maddison, Dominic Solanke, Destiny Udogie, Micky van de Ven, Kevin Danso, Jan Paul van Hecke.

Roberto De Zerbi rested a host of his stars, including Mateus Fernandes, but started midfielder Lucas Bergvall, who Sky Sports News understands wants to leave the club this summer, for his first pre-season minutes before he was replaced at the break by club-record signing Sandro Tonali.

Andy Robertson made his first Spurs appearance as a second-half substitute, being handed the captain's armband and impressing in a 25-minute cameo by setting up two chances and having a shot saved before tucking away a penalty.

Who is missing from Spurs' pre-season tour? Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert and Guglielmo Vicario did not travel due to injury.

Rodrigo Bentancur and Pape Matar Sarr were granted extended leave following their appearances at the World Cup, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence won't take part having reached the latter stages of the tournament.

What we learned from Spurs' friendly with Sydney...

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Tel responds to Savinho news - Spurs are after a new left winger, and Man City's Savinho could be another high-profile addition to Roberto De Zerbi's squad. But Tel provided a reminder of his talents. His stunning free-kick stole the show but he was also Spurs' brightest attacker in the game. If Savinho and Tel are Spurs' two left-wing options, it shows real depth in that area.

Robertson looks energised on debut - He only got 25 minutes, but Andy Robertson made a real impact on his first Spurs outing. The left-back should have had two assists but Min-Hyeok Yang missed from close range. De Zerbi's full-backs in this game were very attacking and often had good goalscoring chances, is the Scot in line for a new wave of attacking influence in the Premier League?

Image: Richarlison challenges for the ball

Gray could be important for De Zerbi - When the team news came out, it was a surprise to see Archie Gray named as captain for the second pre-season game in a row. More experienced players such as Conor Gallagher, Richarlison and Ben Davies also started, but it was the young midfielder with the armband. Despite all the talk about Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali coming in, is Gray the final piece of that three-man midfield, on the basis of that vote of confidence from De Zerbi?

Where are Spurs' goals coming from? Yes, it's only pre-season. But you look at the Spurs attack and wonder where the goals are coming from. Spurs were wasteful against Sydney - with Gallagher missing three big first-half chances and substitute Yang missing two more after coming on. Richarlison was anonymous in his 60-minute display, while the likes of Dominic Solanke, James Maddison, Mohammad Kudus, Xavi Simons and Dejan Kulusevski are still out injured. De Zerbi has made loads of signings in defence and midfield, but more still needs to be done up front.

Sports.title: Infantino offers £30m incentive for FIFA members to back controversial plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has given football associations until September 19 to back his plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors with a £30.1m ($40m) incentive to accept, a letter has revealed.

FIFA announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments.

Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to £3.1bn ($4.2bn) from external investors by selling minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around £15bn ($20bn).

The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than £7.53bn ($10bn) in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville, Andy Burnham, the FA and more react to Gianni Infantino's World Cup sale plan

The FIFA president, in correspondence sent only to the 211 member associations after his secret plans were leaked and met with fierce opposition from UEFA, raised the subject of finances that would be available from January.

He warned that countries will have access to much less cash for development projects, grassroots football and national teams if they do not back selling off more than 20 per cent of a new commercial spin-off to oversee World Cups.

Infantino said the launch of FFE needs more than 50 per cent of members to back the plans, along with his ruling council.

He wrote: "Should neither condition be satisfied, FIFA will continue as planned with the Forward Programme 4.0 … meaning approximately £7.5m ($10m) per MA [member association] for the next cycle."

Infantino raised the prospect that associations that do not back his plans could miss out on the cash if the majority of the world endorses the venture.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Prime Minister Andy Burnham disagrees with FIFA's attempts to bring in private investment for the World Cup

He wrote: "A singular and unique funding opportunity only for those Member Associations who wish to participate, with their decision to be made by September 19 2026 so we can plan ahead and with funds to be available immediately as of January 1 2027."

The letter raises the financial stakes, with FIFA previously saying on Tuesday that the new venture would provide access to funding of £15m ($20m) from 2027 to 2030 - a figure that has now doubled.

Infantino wrote: "This entity will be fully focused on one target objective; generating as much value as possible for FIFA's Member Associations."

But FIFA has not commented on how much Infantino stands to benefit financially from delivering a £15bn ($20bn) venture - and how he could stay on beyond 2031 when term limits require him to relinquish the presidency if re-elected next year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News sports correspondent Rob Harris raises the prospect of the World Cup being boycotted due to FIFA's attempts to bring in private investment

Threat of a boycott and 'deep concern' from the FA

UEFA, European football's governing body, issued a furious statement on Tuesday, saying the proposals "crossed a line".

An emergency virtual meeting of UEFA's 55 member associations will take place on Thursday to discuss opposition to FIFA's controversial idea and Sky Sports News understands there is a willingness to use the threat of a boycott if Infantino pushes ahead with the plans.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham voiced his criticism on Tuesday evening, saying on X: "Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine."
