Sports.title: Abusive chanting against immigrants in English football on rise, new data reveals
Sports.content:
Abusive chanting against immigrants has become a feature of football matches in England, according to new data from Kick It Out.

Last season 39 reports of anti-immigrant chanting were made to the anti-discrimination charity, more than the previous two seasons combined. Phrases such as “stop the boats” and “send them back” were reported as being heard “at all levels of the game”, Kick It Out said.

The growth in anti-immigrant rhetoric was consistent with a broader rise in reports of discrimination, at matches and online. Kick It Out received 1,744 reports of discriminatory behaviour in total during the 2025-26 season, a record and a 25% increase on the previous campaign.

The number of reported incidents increased across every type of discrimination to new highs. Reports of racism remained the most common, rising 19% year-on-year, the 792 reports making up 45% of the total. Complaints of sexist behaviour rose 12% to 216, homophobia rose 46% to 203, antisemitism rose 43% to 93, ableism rose 20% to 89, and Islamophobia rose 88% to 60. Kick it Out said all six areas had seen their biggest totals in five years.

Reports of abuse in grassroots football rose for a fifth consecutive year, up by 33% in 2025-26 to a record 248 reports. Equally, the 98 reports of abuse against match officials was the same as the past three seasons combined.

Samuel Okafor, chief executive at Kick It Out, said such behaviour at matches and in online spaces was matched by a rise in hateful rhetoric elsewhere in British society, but he praised the willingness of supporters – and players – to speak out.

“These figures show that discrimination remains deeply embedded across the game at a time when we’re also seeing rises in hate crime and divisive political rhetoric in Britain,” he said. “But they also show that people are more willing to stand up to abuse when they see it, and it’s encouraging to see professional players set that example last season.”

For example, in March, a 60-year-old man was given a suspended sentence for sending offensive messages to the England Women defender Jess Carter, who went public over the attacks during the European Championship last year. In the men’s game, Antoine Semenyo drew attention to the racist abuse he had received over the course of the season, with a charge of racially aggravated behaviour against one man scheduled to go to trial in September.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Kick It Out’s findings concur with those reported by the UK Football Policing Unit last week. The police said that some of the increase could be explained by improved reporting mechanisms, with misogynist abuse only introduced as a separate category of discrimination at the start of last season. Both police and Kick It Out have called on online platforms to do more to stop abuse.

Okafor said: “We will continue to work with football authorities, clubs, leagues, regulators and government to ensure we match the courage shown to report abuse with clear and consistent action so that football is welcoming to everyone.”

Sports.title: 'Clicky Ponting' is just the tip of the iceberg. I've played club cricket for decades and these are the wildest stories of cheating, from vaseline to elastic bands and fattening up umpires to a trail of sawdust
Sports.content:
'Clicky Ponting' is just the tip of the iceberg. I've played club cricket for decades and these are the wildest stories of cheating, from vaseline to elastic bands and fattening up umpires to a trail of sawdust

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

At the snap of a finger, Brian Devine became English cricket's Public Enemy No 1 - and 'Clicky Ponting' was born.

An investigation is underway in the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League after several videos appeared to show Saltburn CC slip fielder Devine clicking his fingers as the ball passed the batsman to mimic the sound of an edge.

Devine’s aim is as clear as it is shocking – to con the umpire into giving his team a wicket. The spirit of cricket this most definitely is not, and Devine and his team’s actions have shocked the cricketing world (and his now former sponsor, the local curry house).

But Saltburn are hardly the only team over the years to bend the rules – and in some cases, openly break them.

The 2018 scandal which saw three Australian cricketers receive long bans for their part in a sandpaper ball tampering plot and Alex Carey’s controversial 2023 Ashes run out of Jonny Bairstow are high-profile recent examples in international cricket.

And similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level, too. We've gathered together the best (or worst, depending on your view) from decades' worth of experience in the glory, and shame, of club cricket.

Brian Devine, the man at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' club cricket scandal

Devine (circled) is being investigated by his local league, with allegations he clicked his fingers when the ball passed an opposition player's bat to simulate the sound of an edge

Vaseline assistance

Sunny Agnihotri played for West Blatchington Cricket Club between 2002 and 2008, and won the Sussex Invitation League Division 1 twice.

When they met Crawley Eagles, the opposition would put Vaseline on their bats ahead of the match. The idea was that when the ball nicked the outside edge, it wouldn’t make so much noise.

‘We asked the umpires about it and they said it’s not against the rules,' said Agnihotri. 'They were also definitely rummaging in their pockets between balls, so we knew something untoward was going on. They made it so obvious. The dark arts happen a lot.’

Local rivals Brighton Insurance would waste time when they batted first to use up the daylight.

Between a dismissed batsman walking off and a new one replacing him, you had three minutes. But on the field of play, you could still get padded up. Brighton players would throw all their equipment on the pitch and take longer than three minutes without punishment.

‘They would take double the time so that when it was our turn to bat, it would be gloomier,’ Agnihotri said.

Izzy Martin

But similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level too

It’s not always the players…

There was an umpire in the Leicestershire leagues during the late 1990s renowned for getting a twitchy trigger finger the closer it got to opening time at the bar.

When he started to get really thirsty, he would whisper under his breath: ‘Next one that hits the pads… give it a big appeal’ and, when the fielding side did, he duly obliged.

A trick of one former Leicestershire Premier Division champion team was to send beers to the umpires' room and offer them sweets while in the field in a bid to get them on-side so decisions would fall in their favour.

‘Where there’s a will, there’s a way,’ said one member of the side. Their wicketkeeper was also known for trying to kick the stumps down and appealing that the batter had been bowled.

I remember playing in a county age-group match in which one fielder on the team, who went on to become a professional, took a catch on the half-volley and celebrated as though it was clean.

Another team in the Leicestershire leagues was once accused of sending the same batsman in twice in different kit, until their plan was foiled when the star man was spotted by the home team scorer through her binoculars.

Anonymous

No matter the spread of the 'spirit of cricket', the laws are always open to a little bending

Let's all band together

I played in a match many, many years ago where three of our batsmen were given out caught behind, all of them swearing blind they never got a nick on the ball.

After some brief research, we realised the wicketkeeper had an elastic band attached to his glove, which he snapped against it to make the noise of a nick, fooling the umpire into giving it out in a similar trick to Saltburn's.

Anonymous

Saltburn CC, which has now come under international scrutiny after Devine was caught on camera

Questionable declaration

In 2017, Pembrokeshire rivals Carew and Cresselly took on each other in the final game of that year’s West Wales league season. Carew were top, Cresselly second.

Cresselly faced a difficult task that day, but not an impossible one. Carew’s lead was 21 points and a win was worth 20, but then you had the bonuses to consider – a point for every 40 runs up to 200 and a point for every two wickets.

In short, it boiled down to this: if Cresselly could win and take two more bonus points than Carew, they’d snatch the title. But Carew had a devilish plan.

As far as I’ve been told in my retracing of the steps, they even checked the rules with the umpire before the game, found their read of the situation was accurate, and set about putting it in action.

Batting first, they declared on just 18 for one. First there was shock, then revulsion. It was filthy and entirely legal.

Cresselly were welcome to the 20 points, which they achieved by knocking off the chase in just a few overs, but the opportunity for any bonuses had been snatched clean off the table. It was Carew’s title by a single point.

Riath Al-Samarrai

Saltburn weren't the first side to mimick an edge - one of our contributors played against a team whose wicketkeeper used an elastic band!

Bailout

One day, while in action for Saffron Plantationers – a village side in Quendon near Saffron Walden in Essex – I was at the crease with my team needing four runs to win.

My plan was to charge the bowler and hit the ball down the ground. I was still deep in my crease as the bowler ran in. But his delivery was short of a length, so I stepped back and pulled it for four. As I did so, however, I trod gently on my own stumps and off came the bails.

But instead of me being given out hit wicket, as I should have been, everyone at the ground watched the ball disappear to the boundary. Not seeing the bails were off, the umpire signalled four and the end of the game.

After a while, the opposition wicketkeeper noticed something off and questioned why the bails were no longer on the stumps. But I just kept walking off the pitch as technically, the game was now over.

It was one I got away with but I’m not proud of my actions – I got caught up in the moment and should have fessed up. I do seem to remember sleeping OK that night though!

Matt Gatward

Australia captain Steve Smith breaks down at a press conference in light of his side's Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018

Another cheat bites the dust

I remember playing for Eynsford at Chislehurst and West Kent one year in the Kent leagues.

Eynsford were interrupted in their victory charge by a short, sharp shower. After 20 minutes off the field to allow the pitch to dry, the umpires suggested a restart and asked Chislehurst to put out some sawdust for the bowlers to allow for better grip.

The response from the Chislehurst captain was: ‘Sorry, we haven’t got any.’

Unfortunately for him, a visiting member had seen him put a bag from the club shed into his car boot, leaving a trail of sawdust between the two locations. When called out, he had the front to say he knew nothing about it!

Anonymous

No age allowances

Not cheating as such, though by way of intimidation it comes close to the line.

I distinctly remember my senior debut in the adult leagues. As someone who had a modicum of talent and was playing Northamptonshire junior cricket at the time, I was chucked in alongside grown men aged just 13 in a bid to speed up my development.

Cricket is meant to be a sport played by gentlemen - but don't be surprised if you hear a few expletives at a village game, no matter how young the person on the receiving end is

Playing for South Northamptonshire village side Marston St Lawrence, I faced a tough task against experienced cricketers. Unsurprisingly given my youth, I struggled with the bat, playing and missing repeatedly.

I was as frustrated as anyone on the field, but my tender years didn’t stop me getting both barrels from the bowler who I couldn’t lay a bat on. I’ll never forget his words.

‘Just hit it, you c***!’ he shouted at me, his words starting off an unpleasant exchange with my more senior partner at the other end.

I was so shocked to be verbally abused at that age, I could not muster a reply. However, in the years since I've thought regularly about what I should have said.

If I had my time again, the response would have been: ‘I’m f***ing trying!’

Alex Bywater

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL MBE: It's time England led the football world again by standing up to mafia godfather Gianni Infantino - his plan to sell the World Cup is a bribe by any other name and there's only one way we can save our sport from extinction
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL MBE: It's time England led the football world again by standing up to mafia godfather Gianni Infantino - his plan to sell the World Cup is a bribe by any other name and there's only one way we can save our sport from extinction

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather.

All the more so when translated into English: Johnny Baby.

Not that he can be blamed for his genealogy. Just as it is no fault of the immigrant parents who named him that he has grown into the problem child of world football.

That is down to the greatest game on earth for standing by as he plunges his sticky hands into the goodie jar.

Oh, how tasty those treats are now. Trillions of dollars worth of global company investment, mega-brand sponsorships, gigantic advertising and mountains of merchandise.

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws. If Johnny Baby is allowed to flog off the World Cup in share lots as if it were just a pharmaceutical bloodsucker, high-tech upheaver of our daily life or mass armaments manufacturer profiteering off the human tragedy of all today's wars.

Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws

But who can stop Infantino who, like so many Italians before him, has found a pathway to power and riches via the American dream? When that wealthiest of all nations is governed by a patriot who frankly admits that his specialist expertise is in brokering business deals? When the presidents of FIFA and the US are a match made in boardroom heaven?

So, again, who can stop Johnny Baby from hocking the family jewels?

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else. As a family trust in the good old-fashioned way. Caring, not gluttonous.

Time now, surely, for THE Football Association – still the first FA in the esteem of much of world football – to take the lead.

To rally the diverse opinions of anxious believers on every continent, platitudinous politicians rushing to microphones, pious commentators et al behind an organised and concerted protest.

Don't leave it all to UEFA, whose concerns reflect all of ours but who have their own axes of rival authority to grind against FIFA.

Time for THE FA to throw off its obsequience to the demands of the Premier League and revive the nostalgia for English propriety.

Time to save the people's game, which it must remain, from piracy. To rescue the greatest sporting show of all, which the World Cup is still despite all the trials and tribulations of 2026. To preserve the future of football as a game, not a plaything of the stock exchanges.

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) must stand up to what amounts to little more than a bribe

To protect the World Cup. Firstly from extinction by a European boycott. Secondly from reduction into a repetitive everyday occurrence by its staging every other year. Thirdly by expansion into the lopsided tedium of more and more finalists (48 this year, 64 next time, 128 sooner than we can blink). All for the money. All, it would seem, on the Infantino agenda.

THE FA can start by setting an example. Starting with a declaration that they would refuse their multi-million dollar handout if Johnny Baby's plan bears fruit.

A bribe by any other name for the poorer – and in some cases corrupt – countries on Planet Football if it all comes to a vote.

For FA's sake explain that this is an offer from the Infantino 'football family' which has to be refused. For the sake of all us football lovers, everywhere.

Sports.title: Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Juventus swoop to gazump Blues

Juventus have made a £26million bid plus add-ons and a sell-on clause for Chelsea target Kerim Alajbegovic.

The Bayer Leverkusen teenager was leaning towards a move to Chelsea but is now closing on agreement with Juve as they would put him in the first team squad.

Hull City eye Augsburg's Komur

Hull City have asked about Germany U21 midfielder Mert Komur from Augsburg. Hull have also enquired about Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

Reds ramp up Barcola talks

Liverpool have been speaking with Bradley Barcola’s representatives about the France international joining this summer.

A bid is being prepared with Barcola intimating he is keen on moving to Anfield and it is now a question of how negotiations go with his club Paris St Germain.

Bradley Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield this summer

There is a belief a compromise could be reached for less than the £140million that PSG sources initially quoted.

The 23-year-old still has two years left on contract but has indicated he will not be signing a new one amid frustrations at a lack of starting time.

Andoni Iraola wants another goalscoring winger with Victor Munoz already signed.

Man City push for World Cup wonderkid

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now though Lille would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

The 18-year-old Bouaddi has plenty of admirers but City are ready to meet the terms required to prise him away.

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed for Morocco at the World Cup

Henderson exit paves way for Chelsea move

Brentford have announced that Jordan Henderson has left the club by mutual consent.

The 36-year-old has held talks with Xabi Alonso ahead of joining Chelsea.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, Brentford are working to sign Mamadou Sangare from Lens and have interest in Pape Sarr from Spurs.

Potters star attracting attention

Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry City, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa.

The Wales international impressed against Everton in Stoke’s 1-0 friendly win on Tuesday evening and interest has been building in the 27-year-old following his last campaign where he scored ten goals in the Championship.

Stoke are understood to value him around £9million.

Stoke star Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa

Boro ask about in-demand Travers

Middlesbrough have made enquiries for Everton goalkeeper Mark Travers over a permanent transfer.

The Republic of Ireland keeper, who started in Everton's friendly defeat to Stoke on Tuesday night, has been the subject of a number of enquiries this summer including from Coventry who finally agreed a £22.5million fee plus add ons with Brighton for Carl Rushworth on Tuesday.

Iliman Ndiaye is subject to interest from Saudi side Al Hilal this summer

Boro have also asked about Manchester United's Radek Vitek but 27-year-old Travers has been at the club before on loan and could prove cheaper. He joined Everton from Bournemouth last year in a four-year deal.

Meanwhile, Everton have still to receive an offer from Al Hilal for Iliman Ndiaye. They are aware of interest but have no desire to sell, though the 26-year-old has turned down offers of a new contract.

Koleosho heads to Paris

Burnley winger Luca Koleosho has completed a permanent move to Ligue 1 side Paris FC for an undisclosed fee.

Clyne flies the Eagles nest again

Crystal Palace have confirmed that Nathaniel Clyne has left the club following the expiration of his contract.

The full back, who made 252 appearances across two stints at Selhurst Park, told Palace TV: 'The last few seasons have given me some of the best days of my life.

'When I started at Crystal Palace we were in the Championship. Now the club is playing European football, having nights like we did in Leipzig.'

Palace remain in talks over a possible permanent deal for Takehiro Tomiyasu, who is training with the club in Como. Discussions are also continuing over defensive targets Chrislain Matsima and Raphael Le Guen.

Takehiro Tomiyasu is currently training with Crystal Palace as he seeks to find a new club

Bees looking to seal £41m Sangare deal

Brentford are closing in on an agreement with Lens for Mamadou Sangare worth around £41million.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Brentford moved quickly to fend off competition for the 24-year-old from Crystal Palace.

Brentford are long-term admirers of the player and signing a new central midfielder was a priority even before Chelsea moved for Jordan Henderson. They also like Spurs' Pape Matar Sarr.

City teen heads to Leicester

Manchester City left back Christian McFarlane has joined Leicester on loan.

McFarlane, 19, becomes the third signing through the door at the King Power Stadium this summer. He joins Conor Chaplin and Alex McCarthy in bolstering Russell Martin's squad.

New Leicester boss Russell Martin has bolstered his team's promotion bid with the signing of Man City left back Christian McFarlane

McFarlane said: 'As a player, I’m intense and aggressive at both ends – attacking and defending. I like to make runs in behind and can be a bit of a nuisance for the opposition.

'The way [the manager] wants to play suits me perfectly, so I’m excited to get started.'

Blues close to landing Lund

Birmingham are closing on a deal for Palermo left back Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old Dane spent last season on loan at Cologne but the German side did not take up their £2.5m option to buy.

Solomon set on permanent switch

Manor Solomon wants to leave Tottenham on a permanent transfer amid interest from West Ham.

The Israeli winger’s agent has made it clear he does not wish for another loan move, after spells with Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina, and that’s expected to suit Spurs as they look to recoup funds and upgrade their wide options.

Meanwhile, Spurs are closing on agreement with Wolves for Kwasi Senyah. The 16-year-old defensive midfielder and England youth international was wanted by several clubs but will join Spurs once terms are agreed and it is cleared by the FA.

Benfica are showing interest in Spurs left wing-back Souza while Leicester remain hopeful of taking 18-year-old centre back prospect Malachi Hardy.

Manor Solomon's Tottenham career has struggled to take-off since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk

Rovers return for Vaulks

Wales international Will Vaulks is in talks over a move to Tranmere.

The 32-year-old started his career with the Wirral club but never made a senior appearance.

Vaulks has gone on to play nearly 600 games at Sheffield Wednesday, Cardiff and Rotherham before arriving at Oxford United. He made 38 appearances in the Championship for them last season but is now looking to return home.

Tranmere have also snapped up goalkeeper Harrison Male on a one-year contract. The 25-year-old was a free transfer after he was released by York City earlier this summer.

He played 46 games as the Minstermen pipped Rochdale to the National League title and won Golden Glove after keeping 19 clean sheets.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

Tuesday: Man United open to offer for four academy graduates

MONDAY: Leeds close in on deal for James Trafford

SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: FIFA pile pressure on nations over Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell the World Cup - with members given just 53 days to decide whether they accept £30m offer
Sports.content:
FIFA are attempting to pressure their 211 member associations into backing plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - just hours after the FA voiced deep concerns over Gianni Infantino's divisive proposals.

News broke on Tuesday that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion, which the governing body later confirmed in a hastily-issued statement.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says member nations must decide on the proposal by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

He says that a funding package around £30million per nation will become available if associations sign up, but if they reject it their earnings will be almost 75 per cent less.

The letter from Infantino says: ‘The decision on whether or not to proceed with this proposal belongs entirely to you. Should you wish to proceed this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together.

‘Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme [development money] of $2.7billion as previously presented.

‘In total for the upcoming cycle starting as of January 1, 2027 each member association will have the possibility of access up to $40million per member association under this proposal.’

UEFA have responded to the letter, insinuating that FIFA are attempting to bribe associations into accepting the proposition.

'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,' UEFA said. 'This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

The FA have deep concerns over FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared. The Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

Should their plans be successful, FIFA intend to give each of their 211 member associations a stake in the company - which they can choose to keep or sell - worth £15m.

The FA, though, are worried about FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup.

In a statement, an FA spokesperson confirmed they had been left in the dark over the controversial proposals which have sparked outrage amongst the football community.

The statement said: 'We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

'Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

'When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.'

It has been suggested that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, although FIFA claim that has not been discussed.

European Football Clubs, who represent over 800 European clubs, have voiced their opposition. Crucially, the body is chaired by PSG President Nasser Al-Khelaifi and Qatar Sports Investments, who are owned by the Qatari state. Al-Khelaifi has been touted as a potential leadership challenger to Infantino.

'European Football Clubs (EFC) notes with serious concern the sudden, unilateral media briefings and announcement by FIFA about a potential new corporate structure for the commercialisation of certain football competitions,' the statement read.

'As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in FIFA’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude. EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.

'EFC always seeks to work collaboratively and supportively with all stakeholders – FIFA, UEFA and all confederations, national associations, leagues, player and fan associations.

'In that vein, we urge for calm and thorough consultation on all topics affecting the football ecosystem, together with more rigorous and transparent governance processes put in place to protect the game for the long term. Only in this way can we build the right institutional frameworks and relationships required to promote the true success, stability and sustainability of football.'

The European Leagues Association, of which the Premier League is a founding member, added: 'The World Cup should not be for sale. It is not the FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal.'

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also among the dissenting voices.

'Let me say this very directly,' Burnham posted on X. 'Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

One European nation has already publicly supported Infantino's plan, with the President of the Czech FA David Trunda backing him.

'I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team,' Trunda told Sky News.

"Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

FIFA want to set up a new company responsible for the 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

They claim the plans would help advance the FIFA Forward development programme, which distributes capital to member associations. The governing body hopes to increase funding from £6m to £15m for the 2027-30 international cycle.

FIFA would need approval from the FIFA Council and majority support from the FIFA Congress (the 211 member associations) to launch the new enterprise.

Three of the six continental confederations have expressed resistance, including UEFA who released a scathing statement on Tuesday.

'This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell.'

CONCACAF, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean, added: 'CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,' their statement read on Wednesday morning.

'We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

'We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

'As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

'This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.'

The Asian federation have also stated their disappointment at the lack of consultation from FIFA.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

The Club World Cup and men's World Cup are currently held every four years. FIFA have previously explored the possibility of staging both tournaments every two years.

FIFA maintain that they have a duty to control the development of this project, with external investors holding only a minority stake in FFE and having no operational role.

Sports.title: Can you guess the nepo baby son of famous former world No 1 tennis star - as he earns first ATP victory?
Sports.content:
Cruz Hewitt - the son of ATP legend Lleyton Hewitt - has secured his first-ever ATP tour victory with a stunning upset win in Washington DC.

The 17-year-old has been a regular fixture on the junior circuit for close to four years, and at the start of this month, made the Wimbledon boys final to face off against US starlet-in-waiting Jordan Lee.

Although unable to secure his first junior Grand Slam title, Hewitt pushed Lee to three tight sets in the eye-catching match in SW19 - which prompted the ATP 500 tournament in the US capital to offer both of the teens qualifying wildcards.

But while world No 151 Moez Echargui despatched Lee in straight sets in the first round of qualifying, Hewitt made the main draw after a quirk in scheduling saw both of his opponents retire.

The New South Wales native then went on to meet fellow qualifier Marcos Giron - and claimed his first ATP main draw win against the world No 85 6-3, 6-4.

Hewitt soaked up the applause of the crowd as the youngest winner at the tournament since Kei Nishikori in 2007, showing off his famous father's signature 'vicht' celebration 22 years on from Hewitt Snr's Washington title.

Cruz CONTROL 🙌



22 years after his dad @lleytonhewitt won the title, 17-year-old Cruz Hewitt becomes the youngest match winner at #MubadalaDCOpen since Nishikori in 2007! pic.twitter.com/wsni2AbLMs — Tennis TV (@TennisTV) July 28, 2026

Cruz Hewitt claimed his first ATP senior victory with a win in Washington over Marcos Giron

The teenager is looking to follow in the footsteps of his heavily decorated father Lleyton

The 17-year-old most recently made the Wimbledon boys final - but lost to US star Jordan Lee

The elder Hewitt made the four-finger salute famous during his playing career, but in the aftermath of his own win, his son admitted that he didn't really understand the meaning behind it, not how it earned its name.

Two-time Grand Slam champion Lleyton retired in 2016, but not before claiming 30 singles titles and holding the world No 1 spot for 80 weeks in the early 2000s.

But after defeating Giron, Hewitt singled out special memories from travelling to watch his father play in Washington 11 years ago.

'I remember being in the locker room,' Hewitt shared during his post-match press conference. 'I remember my dad making his protein shake… being around him on the practice court.

'I remember I did an interview with him as well, and now sitting here doing my own interview, it's surreal.'

Hewitt added that his father had given him some straightforward advice before stepping onto court.

'His main advice was just to enjoy it, enjoy the opportunity I had,' Hewitt added. 'When I enjoy it, I think I bring my best game when I'm having fun.'

Lleyton was most recently a presence in the stands when his son battled for a potential maiden junior Grand Slam championship in SW19.

But Hewitt does not consider his father his sole mentor in the tennis world.

The teenager has often called upon the support of Alex de Minaur, who he trained with in the days leading up to the tournament, and during their mutual stints at Wimbledon this year.

But in a twist of fate, the pair could yet meet in the round of 16 should the Australian No 1 beat Stefanos Tsitsipas on Wednesday.

'He's like my older brother,' Hewitt continued. 'I've known him basically nearly my whole life. He's stayed with us. We have Christmas together also.'

'Obviously I learn a lot hitting with him.'

Even if Hewitt does not progress in his next match, the Stateside win should give the player an important confidence - and points - boost after a season spent toiling in a mix of junior, Challenger and Futures events.

The current world No 612 has also previously received qualifying wildcards to the 2025 and 2026 Australian Opens.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi offers Lucas Bergvall ultimatum after surprise pre-season appearance as Tottenham stars made to work despite 30-hour trip: Tottenham 1-1 Sydney FC (4-2 on pens)
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has told Lucas Bergvall he would like him to stay with Tottenham – but insisted he will not beg the 20-year-old midfielder or promise him a place in his starting line-up.

Bergvall started in Spurs’ 1-1 friendly draw with Sydney FC in Australia before being replaced at half-time. The Sweden international is admired by Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, among others, and has now held talks with his manager about his situation.

De Zerbi spoke highly of Bergvall’s potential with reporters in Sydney, though told us how no elite club should ever need to try to convince a player to stay.

‘I would like that he stays with us,’ De Zerbi said of Bergvall. ‘I think he’s potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don’t want to convince anyone to stay. Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay. He can find the space if he stays with us.

‘The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad – not just 11 players, especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons. Football is going in a clear direction.

'To compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don’t want 24, but 21, 22, of a high level, for sure. I was speaking with him before the end of the last season, and during the World Cup two times, but now we are speaking better, face to face, without a competition in this moment.

‘Now I started to work. In the last season we prepared the game, we worked in the head, on the mentality, more than the style of play. His position is very clear for me now. I needed time to understand the characteristics of the players. But I would like that he stays with us. He’s very young, a very good player, a good guy. It’s not so easy so fast to find a young player of that level.’

Lucas Bergvall started for Tottenham against Sydney - despite the midfielder wanting to leave

De Zerbi did mention there is room for improvement with Bergvall as he continued: ‘It’s very clear, his idea. He wants space (in the team). He wants to play as a double pivot as a position. I can’t give, for any player in the world, the place in the first XI guaranteed. Especially for me.

‘I want to be honest with the players. I want to be clear. I don’t want to make the first mistake. In terms of position, I can’t give guarantee. It’s right when he wants to play as a central midfielder.

‘But to play as a central midfielder, sometimes it is to attack, sometimes to keep the holder, to move the ball faster. He has to improve. He’s a 2006. I would like that he stays.

'But if he doesn’t want, then what can I do? Nothing. He has to speak with Vinai (Venkatesham, chief executive) or Johan Lange (sporting director). To stay with us, we have to have the right spirit to stay. He’s a good guy. We will see in the next weeks.’

Much like when Chelsea started Liam Delap against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, Bergvall starting would suggest no move is immediately imminent, otherwise he would not have been risked. He was handed 45 minutes before being replaced.

While we must wait to see what happens with Bergvall, Spurs are not done trying to add to their squad this summer, despite their ambitious spending spree. They are now focusing on attackers in particular, and could indeed do with adding goals.

Spurs starlets spot-on

This friendly finishing 1-1 meant we had a penalty shootout to decide the winner of this Sydney Super Cup clash. Martin Dubravka and his goalkeeping coach took it serious enough to run through some instructions before the big showdown.

Spurs' scorers were Luca Williams-Barnett, the 17-year-old graduate who chose a cheeky Panenka, delicate as you like, straight down the middle. He had been shooting for fun during this match as if desperate to grab a goal, and so was allowed to step up first.

From there, Tonali, Andy Robertson and Dane Scarlett likewise scored for a 4-2 shootout win.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored a lovely Panenka penalty as Tottenham won 4-2 in the shootout

Robertson's steady debut

Robertson received the captain's armband when the 32-year-old Scot came on for his first pre-season minutes, and Spurs' new left back should have secured his first assist for the club.

Two of them, in fact. Min-Hyeok Yang was twice on the receiving end of crosses from Robertson – and twice the 20-year-old attacker failed to send the ball into the back of the net.

When Yang later failed to cross at the end of one flowing move, De Zerbi was jumping up and down on the spot in his technical area in frustration. The South Korea international has had three loans to Championship clubs since signing for Spurs upon turning 18 in January 2025.

Robertson continued to fly down the left flank in a highly attacking role, and only the fingertips of Sydney goalkeeper Gus Hoefsloot denied him a late winner here at the Allianz Stadium.

Andy Robertson made his first Spurs outing since joining and put in some good deliveries

Injury worry for one player

De Zerbi selected a young starting line-up for Sunday's 2-0 win over Auckland FC in New Zealand, resting his senior stars aside from Archie Gray. That was partially due to their 30 hours of travelling from the other side of the world, and following a few training sessions which have been described as gruelling under this demanding coach.

But a few of their first-teamers were back for this friendly versus Sydney FC, including Richarlison and Mathys Tel. However, when Manor Solomon was substituted, he was spotted with a pack of ice on his left thigh.

Manor Solomon had to have a pack of ice on his left thigh in a worrying concern for Tottenham

Rivalry resumed Down Under

There was a little awkwardness earlier this week when Tottenham and Chelsea sent representatives to an event on the Sydney shoreline to tee up this Australian tour. Spurs sent De Zerbi and Micky van de Ven, while the Blues sent Xabi Alonso and Robert Sanchez.

That saw De Zerbi briefly reunited with Sanchez, his former goalkeeper from Brighton who he essentially demoted before he left to join Chelsea. Not the nicest reunion, then, and Spurs will face Chelsea this Saturday in a friendly before they both leave Australia.

Sports.title: Turkey's bid to be a football giant: Why Mohamed Salah would be a 'BURDEN' to Besiktas, Galatasaray's private island, how clubs have lost almost £500M in four years - and the restaurant serving ribs coated in gold
Sports.content:
Turkey's bid to be a football giant: Why Mohamed Salah would be a 'BURDEN' to Besiktas, Galatasaray's private island, how clubs have lost almost £500M in four years - and the restaurant serving ribs coated in gold

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Victor Osimhen had a decision to make. It was September 2024 and prospective moves to Al-Ahli and Chelsea had fallen through at the 11th hour. Napoli had kicked him out of the squad and replaced him with Romelu Lukaku. A bleak season awaited.

Then came the call from Galatasaray manager Okan Buruk. Why not come to Turkey?

'As a father, I want you at my club,' said Buruk, a man nicknamed 'The Winner One' – you can ask Jose Mourinho why. 'These fans will love you. They will do everything for you.'

So Osimhen, one of Europe's most coveted strikers and then only 25, took the plunge and moved to a league which has never quite gatecrashed the elite. He landed at 3am on September 3 and, true to Buruk's word, the fans loved him. Three thousand were there to welcome him with flares, despite a flight delay of several hours.

In July last year, he signed permanently for a Turkish transfer record of £64.1million. As he puts it, he has found his 'love story'.

This is the treatment which awaits Mohamed Salah, if indeed he finalises a move to Besiktas, one of Turkish football's 'big three' in Istanbul alongside Galatasaray and Fenerbahce. Talks have stalled but the reported wage on offer is £10.7m per year, plus a heap of add-ons. There is, it seems, a hitch over the shirt sales revenue Salah will be entitled to, as well as the commission his camp will get. His alternative destinations would likely be in Saudi Arabia and the United States.

Mohamed Salah could be on the move to Besiktas - but experts warn his financial demands would be a huge 'burden' for the Turkish club

The lifestyle is a huge appeal; Former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson is seen on a cruise down the Bosphorus Strait

Salt Bae's Nusr-Et restaurant attracts the top stars - Lionel Messi and Paul Pogba once went there together

The Nusr-Et restaurant will even coat your meat in gold for a premium price

Besiktas' fans have limited patience. During Leandro Trossard's recent unveiling, they chanted Salah's name instead. But Ahmet Turgut, host of the Turkish Football Podcast, feels they should be careful what they wish for.

'The price is too much - it would hurt Besiktas. They would sell a lot of shirts and have fans greeting him in the beginning, but if he had a season like he did at Liverpool, these fans would boo Salah,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It would be a burden on Besiktas. Already they are financially in trouble.

'The clubs in general are not managed by professionals. It’s not like in England and Europe who have owners and a professional team under them. Every year, all three of them want to be champions and that is causing them financial problems.

‘These three clubs need to look in the mirror and change their habit of transferring all these players and the money going down the drain wasted.'

It is an increasingly frequent tale, marquee names going to Turkey – and not just for teeth and hair transplants. In the past four years, Turkish clubs have made a net loss of £444.51million, a figure exceeded only by the Premier League, Saudi Pro League, and Serie A.

Osimhen's weekly salary of around £300,000 is only bettered in the Premier League by Erling Haaland and Virgil van Dijk. Ederson, N'Golo Kante, Leroy Sane, Ilkay Gundogan, Leandro Trossard, and Mason Greenwood all call Istanbul home now. AC Milan's Rafael Leao, who is 27 and has had interest from Real Madrid, Liverpool, and both Manchester clubs, looks more likely to join... Fenerbahce.

How are Turkey's top teams pulling this off? The attraction is that the league lives in a sweet spot: rich but not as brazenly so as the Gulf states, fiercely competitive, and with huge lifestyle benefits.

'For Salah, if he goes to Besiktas, a large part of the decision will be that he wants to do something special and write a nice last chapter to his career. If you go to Saudi, everyone knows you're there to cash in. You're not adding much value to your story,' Kaan Bayazit, host of the Black Eagles podcast about Besiktas, tells Daily Mail Sport.

Players are treated like kings in Turkey and lavishly paid - Victor Osimhen earns more than £300,000 per week at Galatasaray

Galatasaray have invested in part of a private island for their players to enjoy time in peace

Ex-Man City man Nathan Ake plays for Fenerbahce and enjoys time with his wife Kaylee

'In Turkey, you have the potential to play in the Champions League and are playing in a top-10 European league. You have some of the biggest derbies in the world. There's a lot to like for a footballer.

'Istanbul is an even bigger city than London. There's so much luxury, hotels, dining opportunities. It's a great place for footballers to live - but you can't go to the supermarket without getting mobbed.'

Bayazit also sends a warning: 'The passion of the fans can definitely be a negative. If Salah goes to Turkey and doesn't do well, and he's spurning 12 million euros a year, then fans will turn toxic for sure. It's not likely, but it happened to Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain.'

Oxlade-Chamberlain spent two years at Besiktas but struggled to find his best form. He played under eight managers and four club presidents, and when things went south, fans turned up at the training ground to share their unsavoury thoughts.

The lavish spending is yet to translate to enhanced performances in Europe. In the 21st century, Turkish clubs have only made it out of the Champions League group stages four times – and the last to reach the quarter-finals was Galatasaray in 2001. Besiktas were the most recent Turkish club to reach the Europa League quarters in 2016-17. Fenerbahce once reached the last eight of the Conference League.

It is an abysmal record given their potential and it would be easy to say, therefore, that the money is the main draw. But the players themselves appear equally taken in by the special treatment they receive, as well as the sheer fervour of the fanbases.

As Sane jetted in last summer, then aged 29, Galatasaray's live stream of his arrival in the city reached a peak audience of 3.2 million viewers. Thousands of supporters greeted him at the airport. His image was projected onto the 14th-century Galata Tower – and he wasn't even officially their player yet.

When Jose Mourinho was at Fenerbahce, they put him up in the luxurious Four Seasons hotel for 16 months and racked up a £656,000 bill. His accommodation, one of the finest hotels in the city, boasted a spa, state-of-the-art gym and indoor and outdoor swimming pools. Each day, a chauffeur drove him to and from Fenerbahce's Can Bartu training complex, and when he was back home, he would allegedly always have the same meal: chicken soup followed by margherita pizza, ice cream and sparkling water.

Players are given a heroes' welcome when they arrive in Istanbul to sign for a 'big three' club

Leroy Sane's face was projected onto the historic Galata Tower ahead of his Galatasaray move

Matteo Guendouzi and his wife Maelle moved toIstanbul during the last transfer window

Former Arsenal star Matteo Guendouzi has been at Fenerbahce with his wife Maelle and their two daughters since January. They share a lavish house on a hilltop with a swimming pool overlooking the rooftops and, in their quality time together, take romantic boat trips down the Bosphorus through the heart of the city.

Istanbul has thousands of restaurants to choose from – one travel blog estimates around 23,000 – with Salt Bae's original Nusr-Et restaurant in the Besiktas district, a popular haunt among footballers. Lionel Messi and Paul Pogba once met there for Turkish tea – but diners can also order ribs coated in 24-carat gold for the equivalent of more than £300.

Salt Bae – whose real name is Nusret Gokce – is a lifelong fan of Fenerbahce and has a strong connection with the club, having hosted players for meals and joined in with their basketball team's title celebrations on-court.

There is a concerted effort from Turkey's elite teams to build an environment which can host the very best. Galatasaray moved into a new 130-acre training facility last year which cost around £17.5m, alongside spending on upgrading their academy and other sports branches. They have also invested in a private island in the middle of the Bosphorus Strait and turned it into an exclusive destination where players can enjoy parties and fine dining.

Besiktas moved into a fresh £86m stadium a decade ago and are planning to build a new training ground near Istanbul Airport. They are currently saddled with debts of around £387m, as per their latest announcement, but hope to erase that via investment in a state-backed real estate project.

There is a feeling at Besiktas and Fenerbahce that they must play catch-up to Galatasaray, who have brought in enormous revenues from four consecutive title wins and Champions League campaigns each season.

For Turgut, the race is a treacherous one and points to a fundamental problem in how the big three are run.

He said: 'They have elections with the members voting every two years. If you buy the members, you’ll be president. This system has to change, otherwise it will be the same thing with other clubs. We’ll see the clubs go bankrupt or they’ll get bought by some people.'

Maybe all the stellar names and lavish spending can propel them into the continental elite and bring them financial rewards unlike ever before, though?

Not so for Turgut: ‘I don’t see any hope for Turkish teams doing really well in European competitions in the future.’

Sports.title: Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel
Sports.content:
Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel

The 20-year-old was compared to Spain's World Cup winner after passing the sternest examination of his big race credentials in the £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes at Goodwood

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane has been compared to Lamine Yamal (Image: Getty Images)

Billy Loughnane was dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulated the legendary Frankel at Goodwood on Wednesday.

‌



The £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes is Britain’s top mile race, the first contest in which the top three-year-olds take on the best older milers.

‌



The George Boughey-trained Bow Echo came to Goodwood with unbeaten record having landed the 2,000 Guineas in May and St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot, both times beating Aidan O’Brien’s Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Gstaad. Just a short head had separated the pair at Ascot and the pair’s third clash threatened to be equally close.

‌



It was never going to be as straightforward as Bow Echo’s 10-11 odds might have suggested with O’Brien running three horses in the 12 runner race.

Ryan Moore on Gstaad, whose stablemate Puerto Rico was outside him, had Loughnane in a pocket with two furlongs to run, leaving the favourite having to wait for his run.

For a moment it looked like Moore had stolen the race as he was able to get first run on his opponent to hit the front half a furlong out, but Loughnane angled his horse to the outside and Bow Echo ran down Gstaad to score by half a length, triggering wild celebrations.

‌



View 3 Images Three Group 1s in a row Billy Loughnane and Bow Echo (Image: Getty Images)

Bow Echo became the first horse since Frankel in 2011 to complete the 2,000 Guineas-St James’s Palace-Sussex hat-trick.

Top jockey turned trainer Johnny Murtagh pulled off the same hat-trick on Henrythenavigator when he was stable jockey to Aidan O’Brien.

‌



Working as a pundit for ITV, he said: “Last week at the World Cup you had Lamine Yamal. Everyone was raving about him, 19, what he’s doing.

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane with Bow Echo's trainer George Boughey (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“This is racing’s Lamine Yamal. He’s a special talent, he’s 20. The more big races he rides and wins like this, the more confident he’ll get.

‌



“He’s got that little bit of confidence-cheeky about him, but he has to back it up and today, Bow Echo and himself did.”

Bow Echo’s programme could take him to France next for the Prix Jacques Le Marois or Prix du Moulin with the Breeders’ Cup Mile on the cards at the end of the year.

Loughnane said: “What a superstar horse. I say it every time I know how lucky I am to be able to ride a horse like this. I just feel so privileged.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“They made life difficult for him but I always wanted to follow Ryan. I knew the pace would be on with the set up of the race. That plays into this horse’s strengths.

“I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe, and I just had to wait to get out but once I did he just proved how good he is.

“Me and George watched plenty of Sussexes back and they always get on top of them late and get going early. It just keeps getting better.”

Sports.title: Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna
Sports.content:
Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna

Michael Schumacher's health still remains a mystery with his wife Corinna keeping the F1 icon's recovery a private secret few people kz

View 3 Images Michael Schumacher has not been seen in public for over a decade (Image: Lars Baron, Bongarts/Getty Images)

Ex-racing driver Christian Danner has claimed there are rumours that Michael Schumacher is now in Majorca - but the F1 great's wife, Corinna, will not clarify if this is the case.

‌



Thirteen years have passed since the F1 great hit his head on a rock as a result of an horrific skiing accident. The seven-time World Drivers Championship winner has not been seen in public since he fell into a coma after the crash, with Corinna ensuring his recovery is kept an absolute secret.

‌



Danner has claimed he has heard Schumacher is living in an estate in Majorca while he continues his recovery, but insisted Corinna has kept any details tightly guarded. In January last year, it was claimed by the Daily Mail that the German is capable of sitting up after years of physical therapy, but is still unable to walk.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a recent interview with OLBG, Danner said: "There are all these rumours he's in Majorca, and they've put him in an estate there, and so forth. When I'm speaking to Corinna, she's not mentioning it. When I'm speaking to other people who could know, they don't tell me."

Corinna set out her position regarding Schumacher's recovery clearly, when she said: "We’re together. We live together at home. We do therapy.

‌



"We do everything we can to make Michael better and to make sure he’s comfortable. And to simply make him feel our family, our bond. Private is private’, as he always said.

View 3 Images Schumacher had his skiing accident 13 years ago (Image: JEAN-LOUP GAUTREAU, AFP via Getty Images)

"It’s very important to me that he can continue to enjoy his private life as much as possible. Michael always protected us and now we are protecting Michael.”

‌



In addition, Danner insisted the fact Schumacher still has not been seen in public suggests he is a long way from recovering. The close friend of the ex-Ferrari ace said: “However Michael looks, or under whatever conditions he's alive – I don't know – I want to see him again.

"The fact that he's not appearing anywhere indicates that he's probably not very well. But Formula 1's prepared for that. Formula 1's prepared for everything.

View 3 Images Corinna Schumacher has been determined to keep her husband's recovery secret (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media, Getty Images)

‌



"He's one of the heroes in the history of Formula 1, so if he would be happy and fit enough to come back, no matter the circumstances, in whatever condition, I think Formula 1 can cope with it easily."

He also added: "There are heroes in any kind of sport that have had a problem and have kind of fallen. But once they're alive, I think it does everyone a lot of good (to see them again).

"For me personally, it would be absolutely smashing to see him. I think that feeling is around for virtually everybody in Formula 1."

Sports.title: Amy Hunt proud after claiming Commonwealth 100m silver at sodden Scotstoun
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt proud after claiming Commonwealth 100m silver at sodden Scotstoun

Glass-half-full Amy Hunt splashed and sploshed her way to a 100m Commonwealth Games medal in drenched Glasgow last night

View Image Hunt added a Commonwealth Games silver medal to her collection of medals at World and Olympic level (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Relentlessly optimistic Amy Hunt has always been a glass-half-full personality. Hunt, who won world 200m silver last year, was looking to become the first British woman to win the Commonwealth 100m title in 40 years. Instead, a sluggish start meant she splished, splashed and sploshed to another silver medal at a sodden Scotstoun.

‌



However, the top-end speed she showed after stuttering from the blocks should give her confidence ahead of the European Championships in Birmingham next month, where, on this evidence, she'll be tough to beat in the 200m – surely a gilt-edged opportunity to win her first major individual title. The 24-year-old refused to blame the weather after clocking 10.98 seconds, just one hundredth outside her personal best despite the foul conditions.

‌



However, there will surely be a twinge of regret because this was a gold medal there for the taking, with Hunt having beaten the new champion, New Zealand's Zoe Hobbs, in the semi-finals. "My first 60 metres was really, really terrible, so I'm proud of how I dug myself out of a hole there," said Hunt.

‌



"It was pretty gross on the start – my fingers were underwater, which was a bit novel – but you have to roll with the punches at championships. I think some people would just say, 'Well, she's not a good starter,' but I think I've proven indoors that I'm a legitimate starter. I can get it right. Had I managed to execute a lot better in the first half, it might have been a different story.

"I got it really, really badly wrong, but my top-end speed is so formidable, and that's how I clawed back that silver. It was frustrating in the immediate aftermath, but having a medal is something you can't really describe. It's so intangible and almost ineffable. It's an amazing feeling to bring home that silver.

"I've now got every senior major championship covered with a medal, whether that's in the relay or individually, so I'm really, really proud of those achievements."

‌



In the last week, seven British Olympic medallists have withdrawn from these Games for a variety of reasons, though most are simply prioritising the Europeans over the Commonwealths. In contrast, Hunt likes a busy schedule. Her 2025 breakthrough season featured a full indoor campaign followed by an extensive, globe-trotting Diamond League programme. She won't compete in the 200m here but does expect to line up in England's sprint relay quartet.

Tiktok embed co"It's really important in terms of my journey as an athlete and my legacy as an athlete," she added. I don't want to go on my Wikipedia page in 30 years' time and just see one or two medals. I want to see lots of medals. That's really important to me.

"We don't get much representation in terms of media. We're not NBA players who are on TV three times a week and everyone's seeing our faces." Cameroon's Emmanuel Eseme claimed the men's 100m in a new Games record, adding the Commonwealth crown to his African title.

‌



Despite the teeming rain, he clocked a personal best 9.83 seconds to hold off Australia's Lachlan Kennedy by a fraction, as Nigeria's Kayinsola Ajayi completed the podium. Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu was the only Brit to reach the final, finishing fifth in 10.03 secs. Meanwhile, Kate O'Connor admits she is struggling to adjust to her new status as the one to beat.

The 25-year-old heptathlete won world silver in Tokyo last year, and a showdown with Katarina Johnson-Thompson was set to be one of the highlights of the Commonwealth Games athletics programme.

In the absence of the double world champion, who decided to prioritise next month's European Championships in Birmingham, O'Connor found herself comfortably clear of England's Jade O'Dowda after four events, despite struggling with appalling weather conditions at Scotstoun. It's a new feeling coming into a major championship with all the pressure on," she said.

Article continues below

"I'm not the newbie anymore who can surprise people. I normally really thrive under pressure, so hopefully that continues. It wasn't my best day, but I'm still leading and I'm in a good position. I was really nervous before the hurdles, but it was solid, nothing more.

"I didn't execute as well as I can in the high jump, and my shot was atrocious. It was just miserable. You can't blame the weather – you have to cope with the elements in this sport. My 200m was a lot better, but I can't be complacent or I'll get beaten."

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr's agent gave transfer advice as Arsenal plot move for Real Madrid superstar
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr's agent gave transfer advice as Arsenal plot move for Real Madrid superstar

Vinicius Junior has been linked with a sensational move to Arsenal, with his agent's words shedding light on his future

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior's agent made a telling statement about his future (Image: Getty )

Vinicius Junior’s agent once named the Premier League as the only league the Brazilian would realistically leave Real Madrid for. Arsenal have emerged as stunning favourites to land the 26-year-old superstar if he opts for a move away from the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



The Brazilian's contract expires next year and he is no closer to signing a new deal, though talks surrounding the winger’s future are being held this week. Reports emerged last weekend that Vinicius is a target internally at Arsenal, with football.london stating the Gunners are willing to break the bank for the forward if he becomes available. The huge financial cost of the transfer is understood to not be an issue either.

‌



So far, Arsenal’s interest is in its early stages with no contact made yet with Los Blancos. It remains to be seen whether the Premier League champions bid for Vinicius, who is eligible to open pre-contract talks with clubs outside of Spain from January over a free transfer in the summer of 2027.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta could be forced to break his own Arsenal rule in major transfer U-turn READ MORE :

A move to north London would come as a huge shock given the calibre of the player and just how important Vinicius has been to Real Madrid’s success in recent years, having played a key role in two Champions League triumphs.

It was once inconceivable that he would ever leave the club which announced his signing as a 16-year-old - that much was clear from the words of Vinicius’ long-time agent, Frederico Pena, back in 2023.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Pena said: "Vini is very close with Real Madrid and he’s so happy there. He’s very at ease, he loves the club. He’s been there so long, he’s kind of turned into a man there."

View 2 Images Arsenal are favourites to sign Vinicius Junior if he leaves Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

But while Pena said he did not expect Vinicius to change clubs in the near future and insisted he could stay as a Madrid player for the rest of his career, he did not rule out a transfer to the Premier League.

‌



"I can’t really see that [a Premier League move] happening right now," Pena added. "But who knows, these things change in football and there’s things you would never imagine seeing that happen. I would just say if he were to leave Real Madrid some day, it would make no sense for it to be somewhere other than the Premier League.

"But will he one day leave Real Madrid or will he be a one-club kind of player? I would tell you right now there’s a big chance that he's the kind of player who stays in one club and makes history there and stays there for 15-plus years."

That suggests he would have sufficiently advised the player and made him aware of the benefits of joining the Gunners. Arsenal’s current status as champions makes them hot favourites in England to land the Brazil international.

Article continues below

Vinicius has scored 128 goals and notched 100 assists in 376 appearances for Los Blancos so far. Meanwhile, Arsenal have already made three signings this summer in Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.

Sports.title: UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed
Sports.content:
UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed

Gianni Infantino has received some public support for his radical World Cup plan by a president from one of FIFA's 211 member associations

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino plans to make huge changes to the World Cup (Image: (Photo by Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images))

Czech Republic FA president David Trunda has revealed he supports Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup's commercial rights. The organisation have proposed plans to set up a different $20bn (£15.5bn) company to run its competitions, with 20 per cent of that then offered to external investors.

‌



Other leading figures and governing bodies in football, including UEFA, have hit out against the idea. However, that has not stopped Mr Trunda, who became the Czech FA's president last year, backing the plan.

‌



He told Sky News: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team. Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

‌



UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament READ MORE :

That aforementioned new company would be called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' with Infantino making it clear to FIFA's 211 member nations that if they sign up before September 19, a $40m (£30bn) windfall would be theirs but failure to do so after that date would result in them receiving a fraction of that sum.

UEFA and the FA are among the organisations to have released public statements on the controversy with the latter stating they were "deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further," they added.

UEFA wrote that the plan "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross". It added: "The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football: it is not FIFA's to sell."

View 2 Images Nasser Al-Khelaifi is firmly against Gianni Infantino's World Cup plans

‌



Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, who is also part of the French club's ownership group, is the latest high-profile name, in collaboration with beIN and Qatar's sports investments, to speak out ."We urge for calm and thorough consultation... with more rigorous and transparent governance processes," a statement read.

Glenn Micallef, who is the European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, also issued a clear statement on X where he he expressed concern over FIFA being "aligned with the financial interests of private entities".

On the other hand, the Czech FA president added: "I was elected a little more than a year ago, and for me personally all the projects I have experienced in cooperation with FIFA have been very positive for the development of European football."

Sports.title: Liverpool forced to change pre-season plans as Reds hit with travel chaos
Sports.content:
Liverpool forced to change pre-season plans as Reds hit with travel chaos

Liverpool are due to play Wrexham in New York on Wednesday during their pre-season tour of the United States, with Andoni Iraola's squad having planned to arrive the night before

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola's preparations have changed (Image: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

Liverpool will land in New York just hours before kick-off in Wednesday's friendly against Wrexham after the club's pre-season tour was hit with travel chaos. The Reds' flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday due to adverse weather conditions.

‌



As a result, Andoni Iraola's squad have been forced to change their plans and will now only arrive on the day of the game. Liverpool are based in Chicago during their tour of the United States and returned there after Saturday's 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville.

‌



But ahead of their second friendly, thunderstorms and heavy rain meant that they were unable to arrive in New York on Tuesday as planned. Not only has the cancellation affected Iraola and his players' preparations, but also the reveal of Liverpool's new away kit.

‌



Several first-team players were scheduled to attend an event at Brooklyn's Skylight at the Refinery to show off Adidas' latest product. Instead, Liverpool legends Ian Rush and Robbie Fowler stepped in to model what the Reds will be wearing on the road in 2026-27.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made READ MORE :

Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Liverpool's clash with Wrexham will be played at Yankee Stadium, the home of baseball's New York Yankees. The stadium holds 47,309 fans and it's a special ground to Iraola.

‌



In 2016, the Spaniard ended his playing career with New York City FC, who the stadium is also home to. Despite an injury to Joe Gomez in Nashville, Iraola will have a bigger squad to choose from.

Ryan Gravenberch, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all returned to training, although they may not be involved this early into their respective pre-seasons. "The three players that are going to join us are going to be [in the] second week fully with us," Iraola told a press conference last week.

"The ones that were [eliminated] from the World Cup, they all - because of different reasons - have individual days for their arrivals, but I think the sooner we can start working with them and they can understand what we want from them the better.

‌



Will Andoni Iraola be a success at Liverpool? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Liverpool are based in Chicago for their pre-season tour (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Individually, I talked with the three of them, they know the main things, but I am looking forward to having them here with the group and to go slowly, slowly with recovering bodies [to the squad]."

‌



Meanwhile, Alisson Becker, Cody Gakpo and Virgil van Dijk will start their individual programmes at Liverpool's AXA Training Centre in Kirkby while their team-mates are stateside. "They will, in terms of dates of training, be very similar but they will start training at the AXA in Liverpool," Iraola confirmed.

"Because of different reasons, especially Virgil because he has been the player with most minutes in Europe I would say, and Cody for other reasons, they are going to start training basically in the same week as the others but instead of making them come here with the team, we considered that it was sensible with them to start the first week training with a small group or even with younger players that are at the AXA and join us when we [return]."
