BENGALURU: In May 2026, the Chief Justice of India made an offhand, dismissive remark about unemployed young Indians being like cockroaches. Ten weeks later, a Union minister had resigned, tens of thousands of protesters had marched on Parliament, and a satirical party named after the insult was the biggest story in the country â not necessarily in that order!Nobody involved in that first remark could have predicted where it would end up. That gap, between how small these things start and how large they end up, is the story of Indian student politics itself.It is, in fact, the pattern that connects nearly every major student agitation since independence, laid out in the timeline alongside this piece. A hostel mess-fee hike in Ahmedabad brought down a state govt. A poetry reading on a university lawn became a national argument about sedition.A single self-immolation outside a Delhi college reshaped a decade of caste politics. Indian students, again and again, have turned small, local sparks into fires. Not because the sparks themselves were extraordinary, but because they landed on reservoirs of frustration, economic distress, discrimination, corruption, a sense of being unheard, that were already primed to catch. Few groups in Indian public life have intervened so often, so unpredictably, or with such little warning.India has one of the youngest populations in the world, and its colleges concentrate huge numbers of young people in one place, with time and energy that older, more encumbered protesters often canât spare â but it isnât that students have less at stake.Itâs that whatâs at stake for them is the future itself: the job market theyâre about to enter, the country theyâre about to inherit, the fairness of the exam or the quota or the citizenship rule that will decide their next decade.Campuses also come with built-in organising infrastructure: hostels, unions, canteens, and, increasingly, group chats that can turn a local grievance into a national one within hours. Students also carry a kind of moral capital unlike any other in Indian public culture: the idea, inherited from the independence movement itself, that young people protesting is a sign of a healthy conscience rather than a threat to order.But structure alone doesn't explain the pattern. India has produced at least 13 agitations substantial enough to, in different ways, influence Indian politics since 1947 â from the 1959 Bengal food riots to the Cockroach Movement. Look closely at five of them across seven decades, and a consistent anatomy emerges: the way these movements start, escalate, provoke the state, and either win, lose, or curdle into something else.In Dec 1973, students at an Ahmedabad engineering college struck over a 20% hike in hostel mess fees. Layered onto soaring food prices and corruption allegations against the stateâs chief minister, the strike metastasised within weeks into the Navnirman Andolan. Curfews were imposed in 44 towns; the army was deployed.Facing sustained pressure, chief minister Chimanbhai Patel resigned in Feb 1974, and when the assembly wouldnât dissolve on its own, veteran leader Morarji Desaiâs hunger strike and continued student pressure forced fresh elections anyway. It remains the only instance in independent Indiaâs history of sustained public agitation toppling an elected govt outright â and as per multiple accounts, it directly inspired Jayaprakash Narayanâs (JP) much larger Bihar Movement weeks later, which fed into the political climate that produced both the 1975 Emergency and Congressâ historic 1977 defeat.After electoral rolls turned up apparent non-citizens, the All Assam Studentsâ Union launched a movement demanding detection and deportation of illegal immigrants. What followed is among the longest continuous student-led agitations in Indian history: blockades, election boycotts, and periods of horrific ethnic violence, including the 1983 Nellie massacre, in a movement whose overall toll has been estimated above 850 deaths.It ended with the 1985 Assam Accord, which set a cutoff date for citizenship claims and promised cultural safeguards still only partially delivered today. AASU leaders converted the movement into a political party, the Asom Gana Parishad, and won the state election that followed.When the govt moved to implement the Mandal Commissionâs 27% OBC quota in central jobs, upper-caste students across northern India erupted in protest. On Sept 19, 1990, 19-year-old Delhi University student Rajeev Goswami set himself on fire outside his college; he survived with severe burns but never fully recovered. His act triggered a wave of copycat self-immolation attempts nationwide. The quota was implemented anyway, and VP Singhâs govt fell within months for reasons beyond Mandal alone â proof that a movement can dominate the national imagination for years without reversing the policy that provoked it.Student-led sit-ins against the Citizenship Amendment Act spread from Jamia Millia Islamia to campuses nationwide, but the defining moment came on the night of Dec 15, 2019, when Delhi Police entered Jamiaâs campus, including its library, and used batons and tear gas on students inside. That single raid, captured on phone cameras, played an important role in nationalising the anti-CAA movement than months of organizing had. The law remained on the statute books and was later notified, even though the protests fundamentally reshaped the national debate.A dismissive remark about unemployed youth being like âcockroachesâ was turned into satire by a strategist who founded the Cockroach Janata Party â a parody of the ruling partyâs name, with an AI-generated mascot. Fuelled by anger over leaked entrance exams and graduate unemployment near 40%, it grew from an online joke to hundreds of thousands of members within weeks. On July 20, 2026, roughly 20,000 protesters tried to march on Parliament; police used tear gas and batons, injuring nearly 180 people.Rather than back down, the movement camped at Jantar Mantar and spread to a dozen cities. On July 25, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned â the core demand met in about ten weeks, a fraction of the time earlier movements took to win anything at all.The five above are the clearest cases, but the other eight matter just as much.s â there had already been other student protests in places like Travancore and Hyderabad â when a famine-level food crisis and police firing on a mass rally pulled students into the streets alongside workers and peasants â establishing, for the first time, that this kind of politics was legitimate in the new republic.Student-led protests against the imposition of Hindi as the sole official language ultimately led the govt to guarantee English would continue indefinitely, and permanently reshaped Tamil Naduâs politics around the DMK., saw students mobilise around regional neglect and job inequities decades before the state itself was created in 2014 â a reminder that some of these movements take generations to pay off, if they ever do., is where JPâs âTotal Revolutionâ turned a student agitation against corruption and unemployment into a national coalition; when Indira Gandhi responded by declaring the Emergency in 1975, students â opposition parties, socialists, RSS cadres, trade unions also operated from underground â were among groups that kept organised dissent alive underground until elections finally returned in 1977., saw medical and engineering students protest the extension of OBC quotas to central higher-education institutions. The courts upheld most provisions of the policy in 2008, making this the direct sequel to 1990âs argument, fought with less violence but the same underlying tension., wasnât organised by any student union â it was a largely leaderless, student-heavy public eruption after the gangrape and murder of a young physiotherapy student (Nirbhaya case), and one of the rare cases here that produced fast legislative change: the 2013 criminal law reforms toughening rape sentencing., was smaller in scale but longer in duration: FTII students struck for 139 days over the appointment of a chairman they saw as a political pick, keeping alive the broader argument about political interference in public institutions even though the appointment itself stood., delivered two separate shocks in one year: Dalit scholar Rohith Vemulaâs suicide, after his suspension amid political pressure, reopened a national reckoning over caste discrimination on campus. Weeks later, the arrest of JNU Studentsâ Union president Kanhaiya Kumar on sedition charges, after a campus event, turned âanti-nationalâ speech into one of the decadeâs defining and most polarising arguments.Four patterns recur across all thirteen movements above, not just the five examined in depth.As the opening of this piece argued, the size of the spark has never predicted the size of the fire. What decides that is how much pre-existing frustration was already sitting there, waiting for something to ignite it.In case after case, the decisive escalation wasnât the original grievance but the visible use of force against students: police firing in Calcutta in 1959 and Madurai in 1965, the Jamia library raid in 2019, the tear-gassing at Jantar Mantar in 2026. Violence against students, especially once captured on camera, has repeatedly turned local protests into national ones and made the state's own response the story.Self-immolation recurs across this history, most starkly in 1990, as a form of protest with few real parallels in other democraciesâ student movements â a sign both of the intensity of feeling involved and of a media culture in which one person's extreme act can shift public opinion faster than a rally of thousands.Of the 13 movements above, only Navnirman clearly toppled a govt outright. A handful won specific, bounded concessions â the 1965 language guarantee, the 2013 rape-law reforms, Pradhan's 2026 resignation. Several others, including Mandal, the JNU sedition case, and Anti-CAA, ended without the underlying policy being reversed at all, even as they reshaped public debate for years.The honest lesson of seventy years of student politics is that these movements are far better at forcing a national conversation, or costing one official their job, than at reversing a government's core commitments. What has changed is speed, not shape. In 1974 and 1990, it took months or years for a local grievance to become a national reckoning, carried by hostel meetings and cyclostyled pamphlets.In 2026, it took ten weeks, carried by a meme and a mascot. The grammar is identical either way: a grievance, a trigger, a confrontation with the state, and an outcome judged by whether it produced a resignation, a repealed law, or just a memory.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'advice' to PM Modi, and 3 guarantees to students over police action on protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday accused the Centre of denying him an opportunity to speak in the Lok Sabha because he held Union home minister Amit Shah responsible for the alleged police brutality during the July 20 CJP march.

Addressing a press conference after the proceedings, Rahul claimed he was assured he would be allowed to resume his speech if he apologised, but said he refused, declaring that he would "never ever apologise to the BJP, RSS, or any other person associated with them."

"As you saw today, the leader of the opposition was not allowed to speak in the Lok Sabha. Multiple times, I asked the Speaker to bring order to the House so that I could speak.

Multiple times, Rajnath Singh ji and others were allowed to speak, but I was not allowed to speak. The excuse was that I said something about Mr. Amit Shah. I said that Mr. Amit Shah was responsible for the brutality that was carried out," Rahul said.

"I was also given an assurance that if I apologise, I will be allowed to continue speaking. The first thing is, I will never ever apologise to the BJP, RSS, or any other person associated with them.





The second thing is, it is my right as the Leader of the Opposition to raise issues that are important for this country. To me, the most important issue today is that our students, people who are open-minded and ask questions, were brutalised on the streets of Delhi," he added.

'Sack Shah, order probe'

During the conference, Rahul called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack Amit Shah over the alleged crackdown on student protesters and demanded an independent probe into the incident, which is being monitored by the Supreme Court.

He also claimed the Congress had gathered evidence showing that police used electric batons, pellet guns and lathis fitted with nails to disperse students.

"They were shot with pellet guns. One boy who was shot with a pellet gun is most likely to lose his eye and may not be able to see. I have seen the AIIMS medical certificate, which shows that he was shot with pellet guns. Shock batons were used, not just normal lathis, lathis with nails.

Where did the police get this idea from?" Rahul said.

"Now there are two possibilities. Either Amit Shah gave the order to shoot people with pellet guns, beat people with lathis with nails, and use electric batons, or he did not know it was happening. If he did not know, he is incompetent. If he ordered it, he is culpable. In either case, he has to go. And every single child who has been beaten must know this," he added.

"We are not asking for anything that is out of the ordinary. At least have the decency to take responsibility for what you have done," he further said.

3 promises to students

During the press conference, Rahul Gandhi also made three promises to students affected by the alleged police action. He said the he would ensure justice for the injured students, punish those responsible for the alleged use of pellet guns, and hold those involved accountable.

"We will ensure that the students who were beaten, maybe not today, maybe sometime from now, but we will ensure that every single one of those students who was beaten gets justice," he said.

"We will ensure that the people who shot our students with pellet guns will be punished. It's very simple for us to do. We have the photographs. We've collected all the videos and all the photographs. We know the police officers who have done it," Rahul said.

"So, you might think you're very smart, but accountability is going to come. This is our guarantee. This is our guarantee to the students," he said.

World.title: Evening News Wrap: Air India crash probe finds no fuel switch fault; RS clears Vande Mataram Bill & more
World.content:
The government says no fault has been found in the Air India Boeing 787 fuel control switch, while the crash investigation continues.

Parliament has cleared a Bill extending legal protection to Vande Mataram, making insults punishable on par with the national anthem.

Rahul Gandhi used a Parliament debate on the anti-paper leak Bill to back student protests and level fresh allegations against the government. The Centre rejected Rahul Gandhi's claims over police action during the NEET protests, insisting only tear gas was used and demanding an apology. Russia has charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism, escalating its crackdown on online platforms amid the Ukraine war.

Here are your top stories of the day.

Government says no fault found in Air India Dreamliner fuel switch

The Centre has informed Parliament that inspections found no abnormality in the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the Air India Boeing 787 Dreamliner that crashed after take-off from Ahmedabad in June 2025. Officials said examination of the broader thrust control module is still underway, while the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau continues to investigate all possible causes before publishing its final report.





Rajya Sabha clears Bill extending legal protection to Vande Mataram

The Rajya Sabha has passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem. If enacted, intentionally insulting the national song, preventing its singing or disrupting its rendition could attract up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.

Rahul Gandhi backs student protests during Parliament debate

Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi praised the nationwide NEET-UG protests during a Lok Sabha debate on the anti-paper leak Bill, calling them a reflection of students' aspirations.

He criticised the education system, accused the RSS of influencing the ministry and alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah authorised action against student protesters, triggering protests from the treasury benches.

Centre rejects Rahul's allegations over NEET protest crackdown

The government dismissed Rahul Gandhi's allegations that Amit Shah authorised police excesses against student protesters, saying no shots were fired during the July 20 demonstrations and that only tear gas was used.

Union ministers demanded that Gandhi apologise and provide evidence, while the Speaker also intervened over remarks later ruled unparliamentary and expunged from the record.

Russia charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism

Russia's Federal Security Service has charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorist activities and placed him on an international wanted list, alleging the platform failed to remove content linked to Ukrainian intelligence agencies and extremist groups. The move marks the latest step in Moscow's tightening control over digital platforms and could expose Durov to life imprisonment if convicted in Russia.

World.title: Karnataka Bank posts ₹418.95 crore net profit in Q1
World.content:
Karnataka Bank Ltd. on Wednesday announced a net profit of ₹418.95 crore for the first quarter of financial year 2026–27, as against ₹292.4 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Consequently, the bank’s return on assets (ROA) improved from 0.97% in the quarter ended June 2025 to 1.29% in the quarter ended June 2026.

At a meeting of the board of directors held in Mangaluru on Wednesday, the board approved the financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. The bank’s aggregate deposits stood at ₹1,10,396.41 crore as on June 30, registering year-on-year growth of 7% from ₹1,03,242.17 crore as on June 30, 2025, while retail term deposits (RTD) stood at ₹69,410.29 crore in the quarter ended June 2026, as against ₹65,786.24 crore in the quarter ended June 2025.

Gross advances stood at ₹86,610.21 crore, registering year-on-year growth of 17%, as against ₹74,267.02 crore in June 2025. Asset quality improved significantly, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio improving by 88 basis points to 2.58% from 3.46% in June 2025. Similarly, net non-performing assets (NNPA) ratio improved by 57 basis points to 0.87% from 1.44% in June 2025.

The bank’s managing director and CEO, Raghavendra S. Bhat, said, “The bank has achieved an all-time high aggregate business of ₹1,97,006.62 crore and a net profit of ₹418.95 crore for Q1 FY27, reflecting the bank’s unwavering commitment to sustainable growth, prudent financial management and customer-centric banking.”

He further said, “The asset quality of the bank has also improved significantly, supported by sound lending practices, effective recovery mechanisms and sustained monitoring of the loan portfolio, with GNPA improving year-on-year by 88 basis points to 2.58% and NNPA improving year-on-year by 57 basis points to 0.87%. Further, the bank has improved its capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) from 20.46% as on June 30, 2025, to 21.10% as on June 30, 2026, reflecting its strong capital position and continued commitment to financial resilience.”

World.title: Navy launches ASW shallow watercraft Machilipatnam at Cochin shipyard
World.content:
The Navy on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) launched Machilipatnam (BY 529), the seventh of the eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Watercraft (ASW SWC) being constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), marking another significant milestone in India’s indigenous warship building programme.

The vessel was launched by Mrs. Goolrukh Anand in the presence of the Additional Secretary, Department of Military Affairs, the Navy said. Senior officials from the Navy, Cochin Shipyard Limited and other distinguished guests attended the ceremony.

Named after the historic port city of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh’s Krishna district, the warship reflects the city’s rich maritime heritage and its historic role as a thriving trading hub on India’s eastern seaboard. The Navy said the vessel embodied the spirit and legacy of Machilipatnam while reinforcing its commitment to safeguarding the country’s maritime interests.

Designed for a range of coastal and littoral operations, the ship is equipped to undertake underwater surveillance, anti-submarine warfare missions, low-intensity maritime operations and mine warfare tasks. Once commissioned, it will strengthen the Navy’s coastal defence capabilities and significantly enhance maritime domain awareness.

The Navy said the launch marked another key milestone in the execution of the ASW SWC project, aimed at enhancing the anti-submarine warfare capability through indigenous platforms.

With more than 80% indigenous content, the project underscores the growing capabilities of India’s shipbuilding industry and advances the government’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative in defence manufacturing.

The new class of vessels is expected to substantially improve the Navy’s operational readiness and its ability to safeguard India’s maritime interests in the Indian Ocean Region.

World.title: Son-in-law, grandson of house owner emerge as ‘dacoity masterminds’
World.content:
KARIMNAGAR

Karimnagar police claimed to have cracked the recent house dacoity case with the arrest of three persons from Uttar Pradesh.

The police identified the son-in-law and grandson of house owner Azmath Ali as the alleged masterminds behind the July 22 dacoity, in which armed robbers looted gold and silver ornaments and ₹21 lakh in cash at Bhagathnagar in Karimnagar.

Police teams traced three gang members to Meerut in Uttar Pradesh and arrested them near a railway station on Wednesday. The arrested were identified as Bhure, 22, Salman, 22, and Haseen, 19, all from Meerut. The trio were produced before a local court and were being brought to Karimnagar on transit warrant, police said.

Police recovered 43.67 grams of gold and 64.98 grams of silver ornaments and ₹2.09 lakh cash from them. Efforts are on to arrest the alleged masterminds, Razauddin and his son Azeem Raza, the son-in-law and grandson of Azmath Ali, respectively.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi attacks government, RSS over students’ protest in Lok Sabha
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) launched a scathing attack on the government in the Lok Sabha over the students’ protest in the capital last week, drawing sharp rebuttals from the ruling NDA.

Also read: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 8 highlights on July 29, 2026

Mr. Gandhi could not complete his speech amid protests and objections from the Treasury benches, even as a substantial part of the address was expunged from the records.

“Three categories of people”

Participating in the debate on The Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill-2026, he began by taking an indirect dig at the BJP and its core supporters by referring to three categories of people— students, those who think they know everything and pretend to be God, and “andhbhakts” (blind believers) who believe the second category is God.

The Treasury benches erupted in protest over the remarks, and as the uproar continued, Mr. Gandhi claimed that he was not being allowed to speak.

He said that Dharmendra Pradhan, who had to resign as the Union Education Minister, was just a symbol and the Education Ministry was actually being run by the RSS.

At this, both Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stood up and said that the Leader of the Opposition had the responsibility of not using unparliamentary words and should continue with his speech.

RSS targeted

As he got up to speak again, Mr. Gandhi targeted the RSS, alleging that it was influencing the education system and shaping what students were taught. “The soul of the system has been captured by the RSS. Dharmendra Pradhan never ran the Education Ministry. The man and organisation that run the Ministry is called the RSS,” he said.

He also alleged that all universities in the country have vice-chancellors affiliated with the RSS.

As the protests from the ruling side continued, Mr. Gandhi then trained his guns on the Union Home Minister Amit Shah, claiming that he was not present in the Lok Sabha because he was “scared”.

The Congress leader made certain allegations against the Home Minister, which were vehemently denied by the ruling side. The BJP accused Mr. Gandhi of telling a “bundle of lies” and demanded that he apologise for “misusing” the House by making “baseless” allegations.

Speaker Om Birla also asked Mr. Gandhi to provide proof to substantiate his allegations.

Objecting to the remarks, Mr. Rijiju demanded that he apologise. “On what basis have you said this? This is highly objectionable. You should apologise”.

The House was adjourned twice amid the uproar over Mr. Gandhi’s remarks, and he could not complete his address.

World.title: Ramp, stairlift make Napier Museum in Thiruvananthapuram disabled friendly
World.content:
In an initiative to make the Napier Museum premises in the city disabled friendly, Minister for Museums and Zoo O.J. Janeesh on Wednesday inaugurated a ramp and a stairlift to improve access to the Museum auditorium.

The Museum auditorium is located on the first floor of the building that houses the KCS Panicker Art Gallery.

A number of programmes, including exhibitions, were organised at the Museum auditorium. However, the differently abled were not abled to attend these. At the same time, installing a lift in the gallery building with its limited facilities was not practical. In such a situation, the stairlift facility would make the building disabled friendly. The government’s aim was inclusive development, the Minister said.

The Minister also viewed a photo exhibition and documentaries as part of the International Tiger Day celebrations organised by Wildframes, a community of photographers in association with the Forest department and the Department of Museums and Zoos, at the auditorium.

Minister for Health K. Muraleedharan, who presided over the function, said the upkeep of facilities created for the public was everyone’s responsibility. The museum was capable of attracting even more tourists, the Minister said.

The stairlift was installed using ₹9 lakh from the Museum Plan funds. A ramp have also been built at the 3D theatre while handrails were installed for the existing ramp at the Natural History Museum. The ramp work was at a cost of around ₹6.7 lakh.

Zoo and Museum Director P.S. Manjula Devi was present at the function.

World.title: No shots fired at students, says Union Minister Jitendra Singh as Lok Sabha passes tougher anti-paper leak Bill
World.content:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) insisted that “no shots were fired” at students during the July 20 protest in Delhi as the Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. Dr. Singh also rejected Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s allegation that Home Minister Amit Shah had ordered security forces to open fire at protesters.

The Bill, which proposes tightening penalties and introducing time-bound investigations and trials for paper leak cases, was passed amid continuing Opposition protests over the alleged police excesses against students during the NEET-UG agitation.

Parliament Monsoon Session Day 8 highlights

Soon after its passage, Mr. Shah hailed the legislation in a post on X, congratulating students across the country and describing the amendment as a measure that would “shield the dreams and aspirations” of the youth. “The Modi govt will spare no one who attempts to imperil the future of our students and will leave no stone unturned to ensure that they face the full wrath of the law,” the Home Minister said in his post.

However, he did not respond to the charges that Mr. Gandhi sought to raise inside the Lok Sabha during his speech.

Dr. Singh, who is the Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) and handles the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), responded to the charge while replying to the debate on the anti-paper leak Bill.

He said “utmost restraint was exercised” during the police action and “it was made sure that casualties do not happen”. Mr. Singh accused the Congress of attempting to politicise a legislation aimed at safeguarding the integrity of public examinations.

The Minister said the amendments reflected the government’s willingness to “learn from experience” after the implementation of the 2024 anti-paper leak law. So far, 52 FIRs had been registered since the original law came into force and suicides linked to paper leaks had declined, he informed the Lok Sabha.

Targeting Mr. Gandhi, he said the Opposition leader lacked even a basic understanding of parliamentary functioning and administrative procedures. He also expressed disappointment over Opposition sloganeering, saying members had chosen to politicise the issue instead of participating in a serious discussion on the Bill.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju sharpened the government’s response outside the House, accusing Mr. Gandhi of misleading the House by alleging that Mr. Shah had ordered firing on students.

“The Home Minister or any other Minister does not give an order for firing. These are not in the domain of Ministers. Such orders are passed by the Magistrate or the SDM [Sub-Divisional Magistrate] present at the spot. How can he not know this basic thing?” Mr. Rijiju asked, adding that Mr. Gandhi had failed to engage with the substance of the legislation during the debate.

Responding to the government’s assertion that no shots had been fired, Mr. Gandhi stood by his charge. “I brought before you a boy who suffered pellet gun injury. He could lose an eye and the pellet gun is a lethal weapon. And the government is saying I am lying. What do you want me to do? Bring the gun?” he said.

The amendments, introduced after the NEET-UG paper leak controversy and the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following widespread student protests, significantly strengthen the 2024 law.

They mandate that investigations into paper leak cases be completed within two months and empower States and Union Territories to designate Sessions Courts as special fast-track courts to conduct day-to-day trials and complete them within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.

The Bill also enhances penalties for offenders. Individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face imprisonment ranging from five to 10 years and fines of up to ₹50 lakh. Organised rackets will attract a minimum sentence of seven years and fines of up to ₹10 crore. In addition, the Centre has been empowered to constitute special task forces to investigate cases whenever necessary.

World.title: Chennai Corporation collects over ₹150 crore in property tax drive
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has collected ₹157.39 crore in property tax during a special intensive collection drive held between July 3 and 29, 2026. The collection camp will conclude on July 31.

As part of the enforcement measures, civic officials sealed the premises of South India Hotels Private Limited in Egmore, located in Ward 61 of the Royapuram zone, on Wednesday. The action was initiated after the establishment failed to renew its trade licence for the 2026-27 financial year and accumulated property tax arrears amounting to ₹8,38,850.

In a separate action, officials sealed Velavan Stores Silks Private Limited on Usman Road in T. Nagar, falling under Ward 133 of the Kodambakkam zone, over unpaid property tax dues of ₹15,91,494. The premises were subsequently reopened after the firm remitted the entire pending amount.

The civic body has directed all property owners with pending dues to clear their arrears before July 31 to avoid penal interest and further enforcement proceedings.

World.title: Eggs to remain on mid-day meal menu in Kolkata schools: WB CM
World.content:
Putting an end to the controversy over the alleged denial of eggs in mid-day meals for schoolchildren in Kolkata, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) said that while the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) will provide protein-rich mid-day meals to children, eggs will be provided separately through self-help groups (SHGs).

“From August 1, as a pilot project, ‘satvik’ and protein-rich mid-day meals will be provided to children by ISKCON in large parts of Kolkata. Along with that, eggs will be provided to children through SHGs so that we can provide protein-rich meals to our future generations,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister had announced a few weeks ago that ISKCON would provide cooked meals to schools in Kolkata, raising concerns that eggs would be removed from mid-day meals at the schools where ISKCON would supply cooked food.

Members of Opposition parties in West Bengal, including former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, had raised questions over why schoolchildren were being deprived of eggs, which are a good source of protein.

The decision to entrust ISKCON with providing mid-day meals in Kolkata schools was also criticised as an attempt by the BJP government in West Bengal to impose vegetarianism.

The announcement by the Chief Minister at the State Secretariat on Wednesday put an end to all the criticism and the debate over the denial of eggs to schoolchildren in the State.

Mr. Adhikari added that the State government has increased the allocation for mid-day meals from ₹6.78 to ₹10 per student per day. The Chief Minister also distributed grants to 80,375 government and government-aided schools under the Samagra Shiksha Mission. He added that all teacher vacancies in schools would be filled, and about 50,000 new teachers will be appointed.

Allegations of corruption in the recruitment of teachers and non-teaching staff at State-run schools had become a major issue during the Trinamool Congress regime, and several government officials and Trinamool leaders were arrested in connection with the alleged cash-for-jobs scam.

World.title: Paper’ ‘leak’ at Gujarat Ayurved University: Students’ wings of 3 political parties stage protests
World.content:
The Shalya Tantra-1 (surgical methods) paper of the Bachelor of Ayurveda Medicine and Surgery – suspected to have leaked – had been put through the two-person authentication system.

On Wednesday, several student organisations, including the RSS-backed Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Congress’s National Students Union of India (NSUI), organised protests over the issue. They demanded an investigation and immediate action against those responsible.

On July 20, five days before a nationwide agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party and activists against the NEET paper leaks led to the resignation of senior BJP leader Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister, a suspected “paper leak” alert went up from Gujarat’s capital, Gandhinagar.

Also Read | Probe on into exam paper ‘leak’ at Gujarat Ayurved University

A flying squad of invigilators suddenly dropped into Shree Balahanuman Ayurved Mahavidyalaya in Mansa, Gandhinagar, one of 26 colleges in the state, where the Shalya Tantra-1 paper of third year students of Bachelor of Ayurveda Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) was underway.

A professor from the Government Ayurved College in Junagadh, who was part of the squad, learnt that there was a text message being circulated that contained “important questions” for the same paper. He alerted top officials of Gujarat Ayurved University (GAU) about a “suspect” paper leak as 11 of the 12 questions in the message were indeed also in the examination paper that day, something that could impact the 2,000-odd students across 26 Ayurved colleges under GAU who took the examination on July 20.



Vd Nareshkumar D Jain, the in-charge Vice Chancellor (V-C) of GAU, said the alarm was raised by a professor in Junagadh.

Jain has set up a three-member committee of two principals and one Reader to internally probe the suspect paper leak. The matter would come to public knowledge only a week later.

A group of ABVP members on Wednesday went to the V-C’s office, asking him to “resign if he couldn’t stop paper leaks”. Devansh Brahmbhatt, Gujarat state secretary ABVP told The Indian Express, “The committee formed in this matter to investigate the paper leak should disclose the names of all those involved and take legal action against them at the earliest. It is the students’ career which is at stake.”



Narendra Solanki President, Gujarat National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) said a representation demanding ‘strict action in the BAMS paper leak case of Gujarat Ayurveda University and the increasing rate of paper leak cases in the state’ was also submitted to several district collectors, on Wednesday.

“In this case, the professor who set the paper is under direct suspicion and the fact that the administration did not take appropriate action on time is also a matter of investigation,” Solanki alleged, warning of an agitation across the state if strict action was not taken.

NSUI has demanded a ‘judicial and impartial investigation into the alleged paper leak and prompt and strict criminal action against those involved including paper setters and responsible officials, to ensure transparency in all state universities and education board examinations so that the future of students is not compromised’.



Similar warnings were issued by the AAP’s student wing, the Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP) which held a protest at GAU in Jamnagar on Wednesday. A statement issued by the party said, “If there is any state in the entire country where the maximum number of paper leak incidents occur, it happens in Gujarat.”

In-charge V-C Jain told The Indian Express, “The alarm was raised by a professor at Junagadh Ayurved College, who was at a college in Gandhinagar that day. He saw the message and informed us. The message contained important questions that could be asked in the paper. We don’t know who shared the message from which 11 of 12 questions were indeed asked in the Shalya Tantra-1 paper. The inquiry committee will speak to the complainant, other faculty as well as all those involved in the paper setting procedure. From the clerical to administrative level before filing the report.”



However, Jain pointed out that the tracing of the text message through various phones would have to be done by the police. No complaint has yet been filed in the matter and the investigation, at present, remains confined to the internal processes of the University.

Could it be a coincidence?

There may be an argument to be made for a possible coincidence that the text message just happened to have 11 of the 12 questions that also appeared in the exam paper that day.

The Vice Chancellor said, “The government has given a blueprint for each paper which has Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ), Short Answer Questions (SAQ) and Long Answer Questions (LAQ). Certain topics in the subject must be asked in certain sections of the paper based on their marks weightage in the curriculum. There are limitations that topics meant for MCQ may not be asked in LAQ and so on.”



Vd. Jain added, “So it’s possible that these questions in the message may be purely coincidental. And it’s of course possible that it may have been leaked. We are not ruling out anything and it is all under investigation. If it is circulated among a small group of students then we will take action against them and if it was circulated widely, we may have to conduct this exam again.”

Notably, the written exams of GAU will continue till August 2 and thus the University has recommended that the inquiry committee limit its investigation to the faculty, clerical and administrative aspects till the students get free next week.

Five Papers & Two-Person Authorisation

Explaining the security of the examination system and the randomness of the selection of the subject paper that finally reached the students, the Vice Chancellor said, “From 26 colleges, five paper setters are selected by the Exam Control Board from among teachers who have completed five years experience. After that, these five question papers go to the Moderator who cross-checks all of them against the syllabus and whether the questions have been asked based on marks weightage for each topic. The paper is then sealed.”



Vd. Jain added, “On the morning of the exam, the VC selects one of the five papers at random and that is sent to all the exam centres. They are sent with watermarks and coded specifically to the colleges.”

The Principal of each college is the Chief Supervisor. The university also appoints a professor or associate professor from another college to act as Senior Supervisor.

On the two-person authorization protocol, Jain said, “When these two people are in the strong room, they receive emails. The Chief Supervisor gets the exam paper link while the Senior Supervisor gets the password for it. It is only when both coordinate that the paper is downloaded at the particular college. The process to open the paper is also divided between the two officials. All this is done under CCTV surveillance. Then it is printed and given to students.”



This also raises the question of whether the other four question papers, those which were not chosen to be used on July 20, also have questions similar to those in the text message that has caused the uproar. This is under investigation by the inquiry committee.

Notably, Jain himself, the in-charge VC of GAU, is substantially the principal of JP Government Ayurved College, Bhavnagar, and was Chief Supervisor of Examinations at his college before he had to rush to Jamnagar to deal with the alleged paper leak and the furore that followed. He said he has appointed a senior professor to act as Chief Supervisor in his stead.

The full-time posts of three top officials of the Gujarat Ayurved University (GAU) have been vacant for upwards of a year including that of the Vice Chancellor, Registrar and Examination Controller.

(With inputs from Ritu Sharma in Ahmedabad)

World.title: FDA suspends licences of 21 food establishments in Pune
World.content:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Pune Division, has suspended the licences of 21 food establishments across Pune division for alleged violations of food safety rules, including poor hygiene standards.

Among the establishments whose licences were suspended were Blinkit Commerce Private Limited at Viman Nagar, Hotel Laxman on Prabhat Road, Punjabi Chef in Mundhwa, Madina Family Restaurant in Bhawani Peth, Hina Bakery on Sinhagad Road, Madhav Biryani in Mundhwa and Indian Bakery in Narhe. Other suspensions were issued to establishments in Satara and Kolhapur.



The action was taken during inspections conducted between July 23 and 28 under the “Safe Food, Safe Drug, Safe Maharashtra” campaign. During the inspections, FDA officials also seized food products suspected to be adulterated, improperly stored or incorrectly labelled.

World.title: IPS trainee sent to judicial custody; fellow trainee claimed he tried to kill her
World.content:
A local court has remanded a 33-year-old trainee IPS officer to 14-day judicial custody for allegedly sexually assaulting a woman IPS trainee in Hyderabad.

He has been booked on charges of rape, sexual assault, attempt to murder, stalking and criminal intimidation.

The accused, M Uday Krishna Reddy, was a constable with the Andhra Pradesh Police before he resigned from service in 2019 and cracked the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination. His journey from constable to IPS had made the news when he cracked the UPSC in 2024 and joined service in 2025.



According to the Hyderabad Police, he came into contact with the complainant when she responded to his Instagram post about his “journey towards success in cracking the IPS exam”. After exchanging numbers, the two allegedly entered into a relationship. “The relationship was marked with frequent arguments, emotional manipulation, possessiveness and volatile behaviour,” a statement by Hyderabad Police read.

World.title: 9 Karnataka officials suspended after video of drinking party during work hours goes viral
World.content:
Karnataka government officials were suspended after viral videos allegedly showed them skipping work and consuming alcohol during office hours near Siddarabetta.

The Karnataka Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department suspended nine government officials Wednesday for allegedly partying during working hours.

The suspensions came after videos showing the officials skipping work and partying near Siddarabetta hill station went viral on social media platforms. The officials were seen consuming alcohol on the evening of July 24, prompting authorities to initiate strict disciplinary action.

The office of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre released copies of the suspension orders issued against the staff. The suspended officials include six panchayat development officers — Girish, Harish, Prashanth D, Chiranjeevi, Ravishankar, and Dinesh B M; two secretaries, Kemparangayya and Gangadhar; and second division Assistant Manjunath. All nine officials are posted in different parts of the Bengaluru Rural district.

World.title: Moshi tragedy: PCMC suspends fire officer for misuse of authority
World.content:
Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi suspended fire officer Rushikant Chipade in connection with the Moshi garbage depot incident in which nine contractual employees were killed earlier this month.

The order for suspending and initiating a departmental inquiry against Chipade was issued by the civic chief Tuesday. The action was taken against Chipade for negligence and misuse of authority for issuing a no-objection certificate for the collapsed building without conducting a physical inspection of the site, thereby providing protection to illegal construction.



Earlier, the PCMC chief had suspended Sanjay Kulkarni, Chief Engineer of the Environment Engineering Department, and Yogesh Alhat, Executive Engineer.

World.title: CWG 2026: Neeraj Chopra returns to Glasgow, but the javelin field has changed
World.content:
India’s Neeraj Chopra is back in a city where he won his first major senior international medal, gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Back then, the venue for track and field was the 44,000-seater Hampden Park. For the ongoing truncated edition, it’s the 11,000-seater Scotstoun Stadium.

But the significance of Glasgow will remain, given that Chopra is aiming to win his first medal since winning his own event – the Neeraj Chopra Classic a year ago.

On return from a nine-month injury layoff after last year’s World Championships, Chopra competed at the Doha Diamond League and finished fourth with 85.69 metres. He didn’t stretch himself in the Qatari capital but will have to do so because he faces a field of strong and experienced competitors.

The challenges can come in many forms if the top throwers advance from the qualification round on Thursday to the final the next day.

The unpredictability of Pakistan’s Olympic Champion Arshad Nadeem, the resurgent spirit of World Champion Keshorn Walcott, the rise of Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, the class of Anderson Peters from Grenada and the experience of Julius Yego make this an extremely competitive field.

Add to this Chopra, a two-time Olympic and double World Championship medalist, and the CWG line-up looks truly world-class. Two other Indians are also in the fray — Yash Vir Singh and Rohit Yadav. The latter is third on this year’s list with 87.05 metres, while the former threw a personal best of 83.72 metres. But given his experience, class and big-competition temperament, Chopra is a medal prospect.

Ahead of the Games, he’s been posting training videos on Instagram with captions like ‘locked in’, ‘pushing with everyday’, ‘getting stronger slowly and steadily’. But how well prepared he is to push himself to the limit if competitors produce big throws will be the key for a podium finish.



“The 2018 Commonwealth Games was my first senior competition, and it was a good start because I had won gold. I have focused on technique, and I want to execute that well. I don’t have any target, but I want to give my 100 percent, and that will be my aim,” Chopra said after arriving in Glasgow.

As always, there is the sub-plot of an India vs Pakistan rivalry with Nadeem, but Sri Lanka’s Pathirage could be the one to watch out for from the sub-continent. The former fast bowler is the only thrower to go over 90 metres this season with 92.62m at the Diamond League in Rome last month.

Pathirage also finished first at the Doha Diamond League with a throw of 88.68 metres. Nadeem had a low-key start in Luzern, Switzerland, managing to throw just 78.47.

For Chopra, his only event this year till now, the Doha Diamond League, was about testing how ready he was for competition.



“My body is better but not yet back to the old Neeraj. There was no pressure (in Doha), so I didn’t put extra effort because I just wanted to participate. I wanted one good throw. I got a good throw of 85.69 metres. I felt it was good because I was not throwing this distance in training. As I have come back from injury… earlier I wouldn’t have accepted a fourth-place position or the 85-metre throw. But I know from what situation I have made a comeback. Step-by-step I have to progress. And for the kind of preparation I had, the throw was good,” Chopra had said.

He may need a bigger throw to finish on the podium on Friday.

World.title: Rajeev Khandelwal calls himself a ‘slave’ to wife Manjiri; expert explains psychology
World.content:
Rajeev Khandelwal recently described himself amusingly as a “slave” to his wife Manjiri Kamtikar, whom he married in 2011. Responding to a contestant’s question on his game show Tum Ho Naa – Ghar Ki Superstar about whether he fears his wife, he expressed, “I’m not scared of Manjiri in the sense that I live in fear. I love her. And when you love someone, you also have a certain fear of them.”

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

“In short, you’re asking how I practise ‘slavery’ in love. My ‘slavery’ begins with making her a cup of tea. If she’s at home, I make breakfast for her. She decides what we’re going to have for lunch. Then comes the evening tea. She loves tea, especially the one I make, so I prepare that for her too. After that, she’ll be sitting on the bed and say, ‘Go get this for me… I’m craving some makhanas. Can’t you tell what time it is? Around 5:30 or 6:00, wherever we are together, this is what has to happen. You know it’s my snacking time,” he shared in Hindi.

World.title: CWG silver translates for some more farmland for lifter Harjinder Kaur’s family
World.content:
Silver medallist India's Harjinder Kaur poses for photographs during the presentation ceremony after the women's 69kg weightlifting event at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow, Scotland, Tuesday, July 28, 2026. (PTI Photo)

Some more farmland.

That was the thought that came to Harjinder Kaur‘s mind immediately after she won the Commonwealth Games silver medal in the women’s 69kg weightlifting event.

The medal was an improvement on the one the girl from Punjab had clinched in the 71kg category at the previous edition in Birmingham. Since then, her marginal farming family had moved to a new house and bought some farmland in their village, and Harjinder’s father Sahib Singh may interpret her latest achievement in terms of what it could provide the family materially.

“We had marginal farmland and the income was augmented by selling milk from the six buffaloes we owned. The bronze medal won in Birmingham landed me a job as an income tax inspector, apart from cash awards. I wanted to upgrade my medal here and now I will get some more farmland for my father,” Harjinder told The Indian Express from Glasgow.

World.title: Pakistan welcomes Kuwait's recent ratification of 2023 pact to expand defence cooperation
World.content:
Pakistan has welcomed Kuwait’s ratification of a 2023 defence cooperation agreement between the two countries, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.

In a statement responding to media queries, FO spokesperson Dr Tahir Andrabi said the agreement marked “another important milestone in the longstanding defence partnership between the two brotherly countries, dating back to the early 1980s”.

“It also reflects the shared resolve of both sides to further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation and elevate their security partnership,” Andrabi was quoted as saying.

The statement added that the pact provides a comprehensive institutional framework to broaden defence cooperation, encompassing military training, joint exercises, exchanges of expertise and “other mutually agreed areas of collaboration”.

“It will further enhance institutional linkages between the armed forces of both countries and consolidate the longstanding defence ties between Pakistan and Kuwait,” the statement read.

The FO added that Pakistan and Kuwait would continue to work closely to implement the pact in accordance with its provisions, thereby “expanding bilateral defence collaboration, strengthening their enduring defence partnership underpinned by mutual trust, shared interests, and close institutional cooperation and contributing to regional peace, security and stability”.

The statement came as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a meeting with his Kuwaiti counterpart, Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, in Islamabad earlier today.

In a statement, the FO said that DPM Dar welcomed Kuwait’s recent ratification of the agreement, noting that it marked an important milestone in bilateral defence relations and would further strengthen institutional links between both nations’ militaries.

The pact was signed on June 11, 2023 at Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence by Ambassador Malik Muhammad Farooq on behalf of Pakistan, and Brigadier General Fawaz Khudair Muhammad Al-Harbi, the ministry’s Joint Planning Director, from the Kuwaiti side, according to the FO.

World.title: Re-polling demand, Form-47 jibe and doomsday talk — PPP, PML-N continue to trade barbs over Mirpur election results
World.content:
PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari continued his tirade against the PML-N — an ally of his party in the Centre — on Wednesday, reiterating his allegations in the first phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir elections and demanding re-polling.

Addressing a PPP workers’ convention in Muzaffarabad, he called on the Election Commission to hold re-polling in Mirpur if “you are not involved in this rigging”.

Directly taking a jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, he said: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.”

Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned. The term has also been used mainly by the opposition PTI since the 2024 general elections in the country to allege rigging in the polls.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, and the PML-N won nine out of a total 13 seats up for grabs in the first phase in Mirpur.

Bilawal’s allegations on Wednesday were in continuation of his party’s accusations from the day before, when the PPP and the PML-N traded barbs over election results, with Maryam saying in a televised address that it was “not the state that decides election results, but the people”. She also urged the PPP to accept defeat.

Shortly before Bilawal’s speech on Wednesday, she, too, took a jibe at the PPP on X, saying: “The PPP, which is the master of the fine art of rigging, is crying foul. When’s the doomsday?”

Responding to her on X, PPP’s Sharjeel Memon said, “This is not you speaking but Form-47. Doomsday came in 2024, when mandates were being distributed in charity.”

Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission officially notified the return of the 13 successful candidates elected from Mirpur division in the first phase of the Legislative Assembly elections held on July 27.

According to a press release on the notifications, the PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats, while the PPP won the remaining four.

The notified winners were:

LA-1 (Mirpur-I): Chaudhry Azhar Sadiq (PML-N)

LA-2 (Mirpur-II): Chaudhry Qasim Majeed (PPP)

LA-3 (Mirpur-III): Chaudhry Yasir Sultan (PPP)

LA-4 (Mirpur-IV): Rukhsar Ahmed (PML-N)

LA-5 (Bhimber-I): Waqar Ahmed Noor (PML-N)

LA-6 (Bhimber-II): Mohammad Razzaq Chaudhry (PML-N)

LA-7 (Bhimber-III): Chaudhry Tariq Farooq (PML-N)

LA-8 (Kotli-I): Zafar Iqbal Malik (PPP)

LA-9 (Kotli-II): Umair Naeem (PML-N)

LA-10 (Kotli-III): Mohammad Yasin Chaudhry (PPP)

LA-11 (Kotli-IV): Mohammad Asif (PML-N)

LA-12 (Kotli-V): Mohammad Riasat Khan (PML-N)

LA-13 (Kotli-VI): Raja Ayaz Ahmed (PML-N)

The notification was issued on the basis of the official results submitted by the respective returning officers (ROs) after the completion of polling and counting in the first phase of the three-stage AJK elections, a spokesperson for the commission said.

‘Product of rigging’

For his part, Bilawal assailed the PML-N, claiming that the party was a “product of rigging”.

Drawing a contrast with his own party, Bilawal said that the PPP’s track record “dated back three generations”.

He went on to claim that “there has not been a single election where the PML-N has won through the people’s vote […], but always due to rigging”.

“Do they think we will allow them to rig the elections in Kashmir?” Bilawal asked rhetorically. “The Kashmiri people will not bow down and let anyone steal their mandate,” he added.

“This is Muzaffarabad, not Srinagar,” the PPP chairman said, vowing that his party would ensure that the opposing side’s “rigging attempts go in vain”.

Speaking about Monday’s elections, Bilawal wondered how PPP candidate Chaudhry Yasin could have lost given his performance in the previous election.

“In General Faiz’s era, when Chaudhry Yasin won both the seats he was contesting despite his sons being imprisoned, and shots fired at him, then how can I accept the results in this election?”

Bilawal claimed that Yasin’s win was “turned into a defeat” when the PML-N seized Mirpur’s 30 polling stations, for which Bilawal claimed he had “video evidence”.

He further claimed that the voter turnout at the 30 polling stations was 90 per cent while in most constituencies the turnout was hardly 40-50pc.

The PPP chairman promised his party’sworkers that he will “take back every single stolen vote”.

He said he was ready to accept defeat but added that “if you are going to steal our mandate by rigging the election, then I cannot accept these results”.

Bilawal also reiterated PPP’s recommendation regarding the formation of a truth and reconciliation commission to address the ongoing unrest in AJK.

“I am not presenting this proposal on behalf of the state or the protesters, but on behalf of every Kashmiri who does not belong to either.”

He called on both sides — the government and the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee — to accept the demand. “If you walk the righteous path and if you are on the side of the truth, then why are you not forming the commission?” he asked.

Bilawal asked the crowd to vote for the PPP in the upcoming phase of the election on August 2, stating: “Convey the message to Poonch, Rawalakot and Islamabad that Muzaffarabad demands a truth and reconciliation commission be formed.”

The PPP chairman stressed that he wanted to ensure for the people of Kashmir “the right to governance and the right to employment” but held that he would not do so by locking down the city. Instead, he said he would do so by gaining power through the electoral process.

He assured the crowd that he would ensure AJK’s representation in Islamabad and at forums such as the National Finance Commission (NFC) and the Council of Common Interests (CCI).

Bilawal further stated that when PPP spoke of employment in the region, it did so because the leadership was cognisant of the “economic crisis” in AJK. He then again took a jibe at PML-N, whose economic philosophy, Bilawal claimed, was guided by the principle that “the rich should get richer”.

“They taunt us and tell us that we want to turn Kashmir into Sindh. No, I want Kashmir to stay Kashmir and let the people decide its fate,” Bilawal said.

“Punjab, Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh or Balochistan cannot decide Kashmir’s future.”

‘Commission’s role exposed’

Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Wednesday, PPP Central Punjab General Secretary Hassan Murtaza claimed that the rigging had “exposed the commission’s role and the robbery of the PPP’s mandate in broad daylight”.

He alleged that “such rigging had never been seen before in Pakistan”.

“In Charhoi, from where Chaudhry Yasin was contesting, 30 polling stations were held hostage, and when the polling time ended, polling agents were not allowed to sit together,” he claimed. Murtaza added that in Javed Badhanvi’s constituency, similar tactics were employed.

“And on the day of polling, our worker Mukhtar Younis was martyred,” he said.

He added that polling stations in Chaudhry Ikhlaq’s constituency were also taken hostage, and so were those in Chaudhry Pervaiz Ashraf’s constituency, where Murtaza claimed he was in “close competition”.

Murtaza alleged that holding the elections in phases was done to “enable rigging”. Speaking about the role of the AJK Election Commission, the PPP leader likened its role to that of Punjab’s Crime Control Department.

“It was deciding who is to be half-fried and full fried, whose polling agents to pick and what polling stations to seize,” he said, adding that “extending the voting time by one hour was done so they could get time to stamp votes for the PML-N”.

“The AJK Election Commission played the role of a commissioned agent,” he remarked. He said that PPP leaders brought the issue to the commission’s attention and had urged it not to facilitate rigging.

“We kept telling you that buses were being given away and the code of conduct was being violated and you only took notice when the whole of social media assailed you for it,” he said.

He recalled that a day earlier, CM Maryam made a statement over “how the PPP had nothing to show for itself”.

At this, he said: “The past is witness that it was the PPP who got AJK the right to engage in parliamentary politics.”

He added that during the PPP’s six months in power in AJK, the region’s then-premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore had accepted 35 of the demands of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) “with one executive order”.

However, he noted that there were two demands where the “federal government was involved or it required constitutional amendments”.

He said that PPP leaders Raja Pervaiz Ashraf and Qamar Zaman Qaira were part of the negotiating team that “begged the protesters for two weeks so all stakeholders may be brought on board, but the group did not accept the request”.

However, he held that JAAC’s refusal did not mean that the state should end the negotiating process altogether and the PPP’s proposal for a truth and reconciliation commission be dismissed.

“If the state had shown some flexibility, the issue could have been resolved,” he added.

The PPP has repeatedly called for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission amid protests in AJK.

Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues — most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir who settled in mainland Pakistan after 1947, which has resulted in protests across the region.

Ashraf calls for probe

Separately, PPP’s Ashraf addressed a press conference in Islamabad, where he presented what he described as evidence for the alleged rigging.

“The other day, I demanded that the chief election commissioner should immediately decide on the constituencies where we have raised objections,” he said, calling for an investigation “based on fact and evidence”.

He asked if the party did not have the right to approach the relevant forum over the matter, stressing that “only the people of Pakistan and Kashmir can be judges of the issue”.

He also objected to statements by the PML-N leadership advising PPP to “move on”, raising alarm that PPP’s “legitimate grievances” were not being taken into account. The PPP leader then went on to show “video evidence” of the alleged rigging.

“In this video in LA-12, a person can be seen picking up ballot papers and setting them on fire, along with 100-150 people who were led by the PML-N candidate,” the leader claimed.

At this, Ashraf said he had brought the incident to the AJK Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan’s attention and asked: “It has been more than 48 hours since we brought this to your notice, but has there been any action taken against this person?”

He continued: “How are you telling us to be brave and move on as the elections are when there are still two phases left?”

He warned of serious repercussions given the lack of accountability for such conduct. The PPP leader then went on to highlight discrepancies in the results from some of the polling stations in the Mirpur division.

“In polling station no.15 in LA-12, the total registered votes were 785, and the PML-N candidates secured 639 votes while our candidate got 12 votes and yet the results show that total votes were cast.”

He pointed out that the polling station was in Charhoi, where he claimed at least 25pc of the people lived abroad and went on to question how every registered voter could have shown up.

He noted that some of the polling stations had voter turnout of up to 99pc. At this, he remarked: “This can only happen when you are sitting down and stamping the ballot papers yourself”.

“This is the story of the injustice I wanted to tell you,” he said, urging PML-N leadership to go to AJK and speak to the people.

He warned: “If we sweep everything under the rug, then people are going to lose their faith in the election process.”

Ashraf called on the AJK chief justice to pay attention to the issue, questioning how the total turnout could have jumped to such a significant extent in AJK.

“You have ensured the PPP was defeated, and you have done a lot of planning [..], but when you pull such a move, there is always a trace,” he said. He called on AJK Chief Election Commissioner retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal to make a decision.

“This is the third day, and you should have stopped the process when our complaints started coming in,” he said.

Azma tells PPP to be ‘ashamed’; Sharjeel accuses PML-N of ‘dictator mindset’

Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon and Punjab’s Information Minister Azma Bokhari traded barbs as well, with Bokhari telling PPP to be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh while Memon, in response, accused the PML-N of governing Punjab with a “dictator mindset” and through a “fake mandate”.

Addressing a press conference, Bokhari criticised the PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying that Bilawal was trying to “imitate someone” without naming them.

“The PML-N leadership never used abusive language nor targeted anyone whenever they addressed a gathering. They only talked about their progress, especially the work CM Maryam has done in the last 18 months,” she emphasised.

During her address, Azma questioned, “Why was Karachi, Sindh’s provincial capital, at the mercy of the tanker mafia? Why does a big city like Karachi have no transport system while Punjab was running 1100 buses? Why was trash not being picked up from the roads of Karachi?” she asked.

“No leader from PPP can answer these questions.”

She also presented a progress report of the development work carried out in Punjab by the PML-N government, stating that in comparison, the PPP should be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh in the last 18 years.

In response to Bokhari, Memon accused the PML-N of coming into power through rigging in the 2024 General Election and said that the party intended to assume power in AJK in the same way.

He said that the PPP formed a coalition with PML-N after the elections for the sake of the parliamentary process. “This is not a lie or an accusation, but the PML-N came into power through a fake mandate; even children of Pakistan know this,” he stated.

He said that Mirpur is called the second United Kingdom because half of its population lives in different cities of the country. “In Yaseen Sahab’s constituency, there were only 20 polling stations, but the PML-N took up to 99.4pc votes,” he claimed, questioning how it was possible.

“The PPP in any situation will not tolerate exploitation of the people of AJK. The PML-N is conspiring to steal the mandate of Kashmir’s people; however, they will not be able to,” he said.

He said in another constituency, 110pc votes were cast — more than the total votes registered in the polling station — and demanded the AJK Election Commission take notice of this immediately.

Memon further demanded re-polling in the constituencies where PPP had reservations.

He further criticised Punjab CM, stating that the PML-N was ruling Punjab with “a dictator’s mindset”.

Memon also recalled the case of Hum News’s journalist Khurram Iqbal, who, he claimed, had been “arrested and tortured” for tweeting about Maryam.

The senior minister said that no television channel could run a ticker about the aftermath of rain in Punjab, fearing they may lose government advertising.

Additional input from Tariq Naqash

World.title: CDF Munir, Kuwait FM discuss regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the visiting foreign minister of Kuwait discussed regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation on Wednesday, the military’s media wing said.

Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, who landed in Pakistan last night on an official visit, called on the field marshal at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, regional security and steps to further strengthen bilateral cooperation were discussed,” the statement issued by the ISPR on social media said.

It added that CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to Kuwait, emphasising that both countries shared a “common vision for regional peace and prosperity”.

Meanwhile, Al-Sabah appreciated Pakistan’s “steadfast support”, its constructive contribution toward regional peace and stability, and the deep fraternal ties between the two nations, the statement said.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with the visiting FM and expressed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse sectors, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the visiting minister was warmly welcomed by the premier.

The meeting was also attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, along with the federal ministers for defence, commerce, national food security and research, communications, maritime affairs, and petroleum. The adviser to the prime minister and senior government officials were also present.

“The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of ties and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse fields, including trade, investment, energy, agriculture, information technology, maritime affairs, and human resource development,” the statement said.

The two leaders exchanged views on the regional situation, with PM Shehbaz reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with the leadership and people of Kuwait. He strongly condemned the attacks on Kuwait and other Gulf countries during the ongoing Middle East conflict, the PMO added.

He stated that Pakistan was playing its part as an “honest and sincere mediator and facilitator” in the regional peace efforts, thanking the Kuwaiti leadership for its support.

Al-Sabah in turn reaffirmed Kuwait’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual benefit, the statement said.

He appreciated the “valuable contributions” of Pakistan — particularly by PM Shehbaz, DPM Dar, and CDF Munir — in “advancing dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the current crisis and restore peace to the region”, it added.

According to the PMO, the two sides stressed the importance of “continued consultation and coordination” on issues of mutual interest and agreed to exchange delegations in the near future to carry these discussions forward.

“In this regard, the prime minister reiterated his invitation to His Highness the Crown Prince of Kuwait to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at a mutually convenient time,” it added.

Regional situation discussed in meeting with Dar

DPM Dar also held a separate meeting with Kuwait’s foreign minister, with the situation in the Middle East coming under discussion.

According to the Foreign Office (FO), the two held a “warm and productive” tête-à-tête at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

“The two leaders reviewed the full spectrum of Pakistan–Kuwait bilateral relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the longstanding brotherly partnership,” it said.

“They also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the Middle East,” it added.

Later, the two leaders co-chaired delegation-level talks, the FO posted on X, adding that both sides reviewed the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Kuwait bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, energy, labour, agriculture, information technology, health, mining and minerals, defence and the broader economic partnership.

“They agreed to further institutionalise bilateral cooperation through enhanced institutional linkages and regular high-level exchanges,” the FO said.

It added that the two sides also “reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination and cooperation at multilateral forums on issues of mutual interest”.

According to the FO, the Kuwaiti FM thanked the government and people of Pakistan for the “warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him and his delegation”.

“He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support to Kuwait during the Covid-19 pandemic,” during which Pakistan had signed an agreement to send hundreds of medical workers to the Gulf country at its request.

The FO further said that DPM Dar reaffirmed “Pakistan’s deep commitment to its longstanding brotherly relations with Kuwait and underscored Pakistan’s desire to further expand the mutually beneficial partnership across all areas of cooperation”.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest, including the situation in the Middle East and Palestine. The Kuwaiti foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability,” it said.

The visiting dignitary departed Islamabad following the successful conclusion of his official visit to Pakistan. He was seen off at Islamabad International Airport by Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain, according to the FO.

He had arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday at the invitation of Deputy PM Dar. The FO said that upon arrival at the Islamabad International Airport, he was received by Zahid Hussain, additional secretary at the foreign ministry.

It added that the minister’s visit to Pakistan reflected the longstanding brotherly relations between the two countries, “anchored in shared history, mutual trust and close cooperation”.

Announcing the visit on Monday, the FO said Kuwait’s top diplomat was expected to pay a courtesy call on the leadership of Pakistan.

Pakistan has been negotiating an expanded defence pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation and investment, the Reuters news agency reported earlier this month, citing five sources with knowledge of the talks.

World.title: Senate panel restricts Islamic banks from compelling female employees to wear abayas
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue on Wednesday restricted Islamic banks from imposing abayas on their female staff, and called for following a modest national dress code for all irrespective of gender.

A meeting of the panel, presided over by Senator Saleem H. Mandviwalla, took up complaints regarding dress code instructions at certain banks, particularly those running Islamic operations.

Senator Dr Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur informed the committee that female employees were allegedly being compelled to wear abayas, although there was no such compulsion for male staff who were free to dress as they chose.

Senator Sherry Rehman argued that no employee should be forced to adopt any specific attire. She remarked that a shalwar kameez, as worn by ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto, was also sufficient for other women, adding that the state had defined national dress for both genders.

State Bank Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmed said that the panel had also issued similar guidelines last year, which had already been conveyed to all banks.

The committee reiterated that it had only directed observance of a modest dress code and had never mandated any specific attire. It directed all banks to submit their dress code policies and instructed the SBP to circulate updated guidelines to ensure that no employee was subjected to unnecessary compulsion.

Meanwhile, Mandviwalla took exception to the non-implementation of the committee’s instructions for the payment of a budget honorarium to Senate staff. The committee was told that the matter was sub judice.

The payment of special honorariums, equivalent to five months’ salary, to various government and parliamentary employees on account of the annual budget has continued to be the subject of lobbying and political and bureaucratic influence.

Mandviwalla stressed that Parliament had passed a law and no court had the jurisdiction to interfere in such matters.
